items.title: Trump jokes that he is not yet a target of the ICC
items.description: President Donald Trump joked Friday that he is not yet a target of the International Criminal Court (ICC), as his government wages a campaign against the institution, urging member nations to withdraw. “By the way, there’s no information that they’re after me,” but “it could happen,” Trump said to laughs from cabinet members gathered at the Camp David presidential retreat, interrupting top diplomat Marco Rubio as he reiterated American opposition to the court. “He’s not trying to defend me. He is trying to defend Bibi and various other people,” the president said, using a nickname for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is the subject of a 2024 ICC arrest warrant. In mid-July, the United Sates launched a major diplomatic offensive against the court — a long-standing bete noir accused of threatening Americans — promising new sanctions and calling for partners to quit. Relations between the Trump administration and the court, which is based in The Hague, are extremely poor, with some judges already subject to US sanctions. Established in 2002, the ICC is responsible for prosecuting perpetrators of the world’s most serious crimes when nations lack the will or capacity to do so themselves. But Rubio said Friday that the court is “an illegitimate international organization.” Neither Israel nor the United States are party to the international treaty that established the ICC. “We tried to get them to reform and listen to us. They wouldn’t do it. They’re very arrogant. We’ve now begun an effort to really try to bring that court to heel,” said Rubio, noting that five countries had withdrawn or planned to do so and that others should follow. Chad and Venezuela have both recently announced their withdrawal from the ICC. The post Trump jokes that he is not yet a target of the ICC appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Le ministre Mahamadou Sana inaugure le SRPJ et la Brigade régionale de protection de l’enfance du Liptako
items.description: Burkina-Liptako-Sécurité-Infrastructures Le ministre Mahamadou Sana inaugure le SRPJ et la Brigade régionale de protection de l'enfance du Liptako Dori, le 31 juillet 2026 (AIB)-Le ministre de la Sécurité, le camarade Mahamadou Sana, a procédé, à Dori, à l'inauguration du Service régional de la police judiciaire (SRPJ) et de la Brigade régionale de la protection de l'enfance du Liptako. À cette occasion, il a réaffirmé avec fermeté que « nul ne doit espérer échapper à la loi » dans la région et que « désormais, l'impunité n'y trouvera aucun refuge ». Selon le ministre Mahamadou Sana, la mise en service de ces deux structures s'inscrit dans la dynamique de renforcement du dispositif national de sécurité intérieure et de consolidation de l'autorité de l'État dans la région du Liptako. Il a expliqué que ces nouvelles infrastructures traduisent la volonté des plus hautes autorités de rapprocher les services de sécurité des populations, tout en améliorant les capacités opérationnelles de la Police nationale face aux défis sécuritaires. Le ministre a salué le leadership du Président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, grâce auquel ce projet a pu voir le jour, avant d'exprimer sa reconnaissance aux partenaires techniques et financiers pour leur accompagnement dans la réalisation des infrastructures. Le camarade Sana a indiqué que les enfants figurent parmi les premières victimes de l'insécurité, notamment à travers leur enrôlement forcé par les terroristes, la traite et diverses formes d'exploitation. Dans ce contexte, il a estimé que leur protection dépasse le simple devoir moral pour devenir un impératif de sécurité nationale. Selon lui, la Brigade régionale de la protection de l'enfance constitue une réponse institutionnelle aux attentes de milliers d'enfants qui aspirent à grandir dans la dignité, la sécurité et le respect de leurs droits. Abordant les missions du Service régional de la police judiciaire, le ministre a souligné que sa création répond à une exigence stratégique majeure dans la lutte contre le terrorisme. « Le terrorisme ne se développe jamais de manière isolée. Il s'alimente à travers des réseaux criminels qui assurent son financement et renforcent ses capacités opérationnelles », a-t-il expliqué. Grâce à cette nouvelle structure, le Liptako dispose désormais de capacités accrues d'investigation pour conduire des enquêtes complexes et démanteler les réseaux criminels qui soutiennent les groupes terroristes. Le ministre a, par ailleurs, exhorté les agents affectés dans ces deux services à faire preuve de rigueur, d'intégrité et de professionnalisme dans l'accomplissement de leurs missions. Le directeur régional de la Police nationale du Liptako et du Soum, le camarade El Hadj Namagna Traoré, a rassuré que ces deux infrastructures feront l'objet d'une utilisation responsable au bénéfice des populations. Selon lui, ces nouveaux bâtiments permettront d'accroître significativement les capacités d'accueil des services et d'améliorer la qualité des prestations offertes aux usagers. Pour sa part, la deuxième vice-présidente de la Délégation spéciale communale de Dori, la camarade Fatimata Dicko, a renouvelé l'engagement des populations à accompagner les Forces de défense et de sécurité, ainsi que les Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP). Elle a rappelé qu'« aucune nation ne peut être libre sans la protection de ses citoyens, surtout de ses enfants », tout en invitant les populations à poursuivre leur collaboration avec les forces engagées dans la reconquête du territoire. En inaugurant le Service régional de la police judiciaire et la Brigade régionale de la protection de l'enfance, les autorités burkinabè entendent renforcer la lutte contre la criminalité, protéger les couches les plus vulnérables et consolider la présence de l'État dans la région du Liptako, dans un contexte marqué par les défis sécuritaires. items.title: Marruecos manda parar el éxodo de 50.000 migrantes sobre Ceuta
items.description: Rabat ha mandado parar este viernes el é xodo de más de 50.000 migrantes irregulares, en su mayoría hombres jóvenes marroquíes, desencadenado la víspera en la ciudad autónoma española de Ceuta, en un reflujo de retorno casi completo al término de la jornada en el paso de Fnideq (la antigua Castillejos), la parte de la frontera terrestre correspondiente al país magrebí. La creciente llegada de centenares de indocumentados a nado hasta la costa ceutí acumulada hasta el pasado lunes se multiplicó exponencialmente el jueves, en la mayor crisis diplomática con Marruecos y cinco veces más amplia que la registrada también en Ceuta en mayo de 2021 por la hospitalización en secreto en España del líder del Frente Polisario, Brahim Gali. Esta Marcha Verde de baja intensidad se ha producido sin una orden de mando conocida ni una causa explícita, al menos por ahora. Pero resulta claro que la patente inhibición inicial de las fuerzas de seguridad marroquíes ha amplificado hasta cotas inquietantes, cuyos embates se han sentido en toda Europa, la magnitud de una crisis aparentemente organizada desde el eco de las redes sociales. Este viernes habían regresado 48.500 de las 50.000 que habían llegado a entrar. Seguir leyendo

items.title: ‘Picking Atiku as vice president greatest mistake of my life’ – Obasanjo
items.description: By Benjamin Njoku Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has described his decision to pick Alhaji Atiku Abubakar as running mate in the 1999 presidential election as the biggest mistake of his life. Obasanjo made the statement on Friday in Lagos during a fireside chat with maverick musician and activist Charly Boy. The event was held to unveil Charly Boy’s foundation and his memoir, “999: A Memoir in Tribute to Late Justice Chukwudifu Oputa”. According to Obasanjo, with hindsight he would not have chosen Atiku as vice president. “I would say the greatest mistake I made was picking Atiku Abubakar as my vice president in 1999,” he said. The former president added that he was thankful God did not allow Atiku’s actions and overreactions to derail his administration or distract him from governing the country. “There is no bitterness in me over what happened,” Obasanjo said. “Despite everything, I was able to achieve what I set out to achieve while in power.” He also addressed the long-running controversy about his roots, stating that his parents hailed from Abeokuta, the Ogun State capital. “I still know our family house there,” he said. The event attracted prominent figures including Chief Emeka Anyaoku, former Secretary-General of the Commonwealth; Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the National Democratic Congress, NDC; business mogul Leo Stan Ekeh, who donated N20 million each on behalf of Obasanjo and Chief Emeka Anyaoku; book reviewer Dr Austin Tam-George; and veteran broadcaster Bisi Olatilo, among other dignitaries. Obasanjo and Atiku ran together on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, and served from 1999 to 2007. Their relationship later became strained due to political differences during their second term in office. items.title: Boulgou/Justice : l’audience foraine de Komtoèga rapproche davantage la justice des citoyens
items.description: Boulgou/Justice : l'audience foraine de Komtoèga rapproche davantage la justice des citoyens Komtoèga, le 30 juillet 2026 (AIB)-Le Tribunal de grande instance (TGI) de Tenkodogo a achevé, ce jeudi 30 juillet 2026 à Komtoèga, une audience foraine de la chambre correctionnelle, présidée par le président du tribunal, le camarade K. Raymond Sanogo. Organisée les 29 et 30 juillet, cette initiative vise à rapprocher le service public de la justice des populations, à renforcer leur confiance envers l'institution judiciaire et à favoriser une meilleure connaissance de leurs droits. Instituées pour rapprocher les juridictions des citoyens, les audiences foraines ont pour objectif de sensibiliser les populations à l'organisation, au fonctionnement et aux missions de la justice. Elles visent également à encourager les citoyens à saisir les juridictions compétentes en cas de violation de leurs droits, plutôt que de recourir à la justice privée ou à l'autodéfense. Au cours de la première journée, la chambre correctionnelle a examiné plusieurs dossiers relatifs aux violences basées sur le genre (VBG), aux conflits fonciers, ainsi qu'à des requêtes portant sur la rectification d'actes d'état civil. Douze dossiers avaient été inscrits, dont dix jugés et deux renvoyés. La deuxième journée s'est ouverte dès 8 heures avec la poursuite du traitement des requêtes et des demandes de rectification d'actes d'état civil dans les bureaux de la mairie de Komtoèga, au bénéfice de nombreux citoyens venus régulariser leur situation administrative. Parallèlement, l'audience correctionnelle s'est tenue dans la salle de conférence de la mairie. Treize dossiers étaient inscrits au rôle, dont neuf ont été jugés et quatre renvoyés. Les affaires examinées portaient notamment sur des cas d'excès de vitesse et de défaut de maîtrise, de refus délibéré d'exécuter une décision de justice, de vol, d'usurpation de titre, d'homicide involontaire, de destruction involontaire de biens et d'escroquerie. À l'issue des audiences, les juridictions ont prononcé des peines allant de simples amendes de 25 000 francs CFA à une condamnation de 2 millions de francs CFA d'amende assortie de 36 mois d’emprisonnement ferme. Les autres peines privatives de liberté variaient de deux à six mois, selon la gravité des faits reprochés. Avant de lever l'audience, le président de séance a rappelé aux personnes condamnées qu'elles disposent d'un délai de dix jours pour interjeter appel si elles contestent les décisions rendues. Passé ce délai, les jugements deviendront définitifs. En prélude à cette audience foraine, le Tribunal de grande instance de Tenkodogo, avec l'appui de l'Agence belge de développement, avait organisé, les 27 et 28 juillet 2026 à Komtoèga, deux journées de sensibilisation au profit des populations. Les échanges, modérés par le secrétaire général de la province du Boulgou, ont porté sur la loi relative au Faso Bu-kaoré, la prise en charge judiciaire des cas de violences basées sur le genre, le mécanisme d'assistance judiciaire en faveur des personnes vulnérables, ainsi que le rôle du Mouvement burkinabè des droits de l'homme et des peuples (MBDHP) dans l'accompagnement et l'orientation des personnes vulnérables. À travers cette audience foraine, le Tribunal de grande instance de Tenkodogo réaffirme son engagement à rendre la justice plus accessible, plus proche des citoyens, et à renforcer la culture du recours aux voies légales pour le règlement des litiges. Agence d'Information du Burkina DS/SM/ata

items.title: RANA asks Parliament to restrict MP Yakubu Mohammed child engagements until safeguarding training is completed
items.description: A human rights organisation, Rights Accountability Network Africa (RANA), has called on Ahafo Ano South East Member of Parliament Yakubu Mohammed to undergo accredited training in child safeguarding, child rights and appropriate adult-child boundaries following remarks he made to a primary school pupil during an educational visit to Parliament. The organisation has also asked Parliament to prevent the MP from taking part in official engagements involving visiting children or school groups until the training is completed. RANA said the measure is necessary to ensure that public officials understand appropriate communication and behavioural standards when interacting with minors. “The Member concerned should undertake accredited training in child safeguarding, child rights, appropriate adult-child boundaries and gender-sensitive public communication. Until that training is completed, he should not undertake an official parliamentary role involving direct engagement with visiting children or school groups,” the organisation stated. The call follows a widely circulated video in which Mr Yakubu Mohammed is seen telling a female primary school pupil during a parliamentary visit: “You’re very beautiful. When you grow up, I’ll marry you. So she’s my wife.” The MP later encouraged the pupil to aspire to become a Member of Parliament. The remarks triggered public criticism, with some child rights advocates and members of the public describing them as inappropriate. Mr Yakubu Mohammed subsequently issued an unreserved apology, explaining that his comment was influenced by the traditional joking relationship between the Mossi and Dagomba communities. “I sincerely regret my choice of words and render my unreserved and unqualified apology to the relevant authorities, the school authorities, the pupil, her parents and family, and the general public,” he said. While acknowledging the apology, RANA said the incident should lead to broader institutional reforms within Parliament. “An apology is not a safeguarding policy,” the organisation stated, arguing that while an apology addresses the conduct of an individual, it does not resolve questions about institutional responsibility. RANA said children who visit Parliament must be treated first as children, citizens and future leaders, rather than being placed in situations involving inappropriate adult-child references. “A child who enters Parliament should be received first as a child, a citizen and a possible future leader—not publicly placed within a romantic or matrimonial relationship with an adult politician,” the group said. The organisation has also called on Parliament to establish comprehensive child safeguarding protocols covering school visits, youth programmes, privacy, photography, consent, reporting procedures and professional boundaries. It wants mandatory safeguarding orientation for all Members of Parliament and parliamentary staff involved in activities involving children. RANA further called for the creation of a clearly identifiable safeguarding focal point where pupils, parents, teachers and schools can confidentially report concerns. The group also urged government to develop minimum child safeguarding standards across public institutions, including ministries, departments, agencies, local assemblies and state programmes involving children. It cautioned against exposing the pupil involved in the controversy to further public scrutiny, saying the child should not become collateral damage in an adult political debate. “This is not the child’s scandal. She must not become collateral damage in an adult political controversy,” RANA stated. The organisation has requested a substantive response from Parliament within fourteen working days, insisting that the focus should shift from the individual controversy to strengthening protections for children in public spaces.

Cette visite de courtoisie, qui constitue le premier contact officiel entre le bureau provincial du RISA et l'administration provinciale, s'inscrit dans une dynamique de renforcement du dialogue institutionnel et de collaboration pour le développement du Boulgou. items.description: Human rights Civil Society Organisation, Rights Accountability Network Africa (RANA) has urged authorities and the public to protect the identity and dignity of the schoolgirl at the centre of controversy following comments made by Ahafo Ano South East MP Yakubu Mohammed during a visit to Parliament. The organisation said the child should not become the focus of political debate or public commentary following the incident. RANA said children involved in public engagements require special protection, especially when controversies involving adults emerge. “The pupil’s identity, school, family and apparent reaction should not be endlessly republished for partisan advantage or public entertainment,” the organisation stated. The group said the incident should instead prompt discussions about institutional responsibility and how public spaces such as Parliament receive children. During the educational visit, the MP told the pupil, “You’re very beautiful. When you grow up, I’ll marry you. So she’s my wife.” The MP later apologised and attributed the comment to a traditional joking relationship between the Mossi and Dagomba communities. While acknowledging the apology, RANA said the matter should not end there, arguing that institutions must establish systems that prevent similar situations. “An apology may close the personal controversy. Only reform can close the institutional gap which the controversy has exposed,” the organisation said. RANA has therefore called on Parliament to introduce child safeguarding protocols covering school visits, communication with minors, privacy, consent and reporting procedures. The organisation maintained that protecting the child while improving institutional safeguards should be the priority moving forward.

items.title: Kourittenta/Cadre de concertation communal : Les acteurs de développement échangent pour mieux orienter les interventions sur le terrain
items.description: BURKINA-KOURITTENGA-CADRE-CONCERTATION-COMMUNAL Kourittenta/Cadre de concertation communal : Les acteurs de développement échangent pour mieux orienter les interventions sur le terrain Koupéla, 31 juil. 2026 (AIB)-Le Président de la délégation spéciale (PDS) de la commune de Koupéla, Moumouni Sagnon a présidé ce vendredi 31 juillet 2026, la première session ordinaire du Cadre de concertation communal (CCCo) de l’année 2026. Cette rencontre était consacrée à la validation du rapport provisoire de la cartographie des intervenants et des interventions dans la commune. La première session ordinaire du Cadre de concertation communal (CCCo) de l’année 2026 de Koupéla, a été financé par l’Agence Belge de Coopération Internationale (Enabel) et de l’appui technique de la Direction régionale de l’économie et de la planification du Nakambé (DREP-Nakambé). La rencontre a entre autres, permis de présenter le rapport provisoire de la cartographie des acteurs et des interventions aux parties prenantes de la commune, de recueillir les observations et contribution techniques des participants et de compléter les informations relatives aux acteurs et à leurs domaines d’intervention. L’objectif CCCo est de renforcer la gouvernance territoriale à travers une meilleure coordination des actions de développement dans l’espace communal. La session a réuni les membres statutaires dudit Cadre, les membres de la délégation spéciale de la commune, les services techniques déconcentrés de l’Etat, les Organisations non gouvernementales (ONG), les associations et les projets et programmes intervenant dans la commune. « Nous avons voulu de ce cadre que les acteurs puissent travailler en synergie en adoptant une approche partenariale afin que les actions soient mieux coordonnées sur le terrain au bénéfice des populations. », a indiqué le Chef de service suivi des investissements à la DREP-Nakambé, Rock Parfait Ouédraogo. Il a ajouté que la cartographie donne une vision globale sur les acteurs intervenants et leurs domaines d’intervention qui permettra une meilleure répartition spatiale des interventions. Pour le Président de la délégation spéciale (PDS) de la commune de Koupéla, Moumouni Sagnon, au vue de la mobilisation et au regard de la participation aux échanges, cela témoigne de l’intérêt accordé par les acteurs à ce document. Tout en saluant l’engagement des partenaires et les acteurs locaux, il a fait savoir que l’objectif visé par la tenue de cette session est atteint. Le PDS a souhaité à ce que les acteurs puissent continuer de faire valoir leur contribution afin de favoriser la tenue régulière des cadres de ce genre et d’échanger autour des questions de développement. Agence d’information du Burkina AWS/HB/OO

items.title: Family of Bukom crash victim visits Gender Minister ahead of funeral
items.description: The family of the late Esther Arthur, one of the victims of the tragic Bukom Junction accident, has paid a courtesy visit to the Minister of Gender, Children and Social Protection to formally invite her to Esther’s funeral scheduled for Tuesday, August 4. During the visit, the Ministry expressed sympathy to the bereaved family and acknowledged the pain caused by the tragic loss. The Ministry also revealed that it has engaged the National Security Secretariat to assist in efforts to remove graphic images of Esther’s lifeless body circulating online. According to the Ministry, steps are being taken to protect the dignity of the deceased and prevent further circulation of distressing images that could cause additional trauma to the family. The family’s funeral arrangements will also be forwarded to the offices of the President and Vice President for their consideration and any possible support that may be extended. The Ministry assured the family of its continued engagement as they prepare to lay Esther to rest. Esther was among pedestrians who lost their lives after a vehicle reportedly suffered brake failure and crashed into people gathered along the roadside at Bukom Junction in the Ga Mashie area of Accra on Monday, July 27. According to eyewitness accounts, the driver lost control of the vehicle after an apparent brake failure, causing it to veer off the road and crash into pedestrians before ramming into a nearby building. Esther, who was reportedly withdrawing money by the roadside at the time, was caught in the path of the vehicle. The impact pushed the car into the structure, leaving her trapped under the debris. She was later confirmed dead at the scene. The accident also left about seven other people injured, including a pregnant woman, who were rushed for medical attention. As the family prepares to lay Esther to rest, they have continued to seek support and solidarity from well-wishers, including the Gender Minister, through the formal invitation.

items.title: An apology is not a safeguarding policy – RANA demands Parliament’s action over MP’s comment to schoolgirl
items.description: A Civil Society Organisation, Rights Accountability Network Africa (RANA), has called on Parliament to introduce comprehensive child safeguarding standards after remarks made by Ahafo Ano South East MP Yakubu Mohammed to a primary school pupil during an educational visit sparked public debate. The organisation says the incident has exposed gaps in how public institutions protect children who interact with political leaders and other public officials. In a statement, RANA argued that Parliament is not only a legislative chamber but also a civic space regularly visited by schoolchildren, students and members of the public, making formal safeguarding measures necessary. “The precincts of Parliament are not occupied by legislators alone. They are an active civic space through which schoolchildren, students, petitioners, persons with disabilities and other members of the public regularly pass,” the group said. The concerns follow comments by the MP during a school visit, where he told a female pupil: “You’re very beautiful. When you grow up, I’ll marry you. So she’s my wife.” Although the MP later apologised and explained that the comment was linked to a traditional joking relationship between the Mossi and Dagomba communities, RANA said cultural explanations should not override concerns about appropriate boundaries between adults and children. The organisation said the incident should trigger broader institutional reforms rather than end with an apology. “An apology is not a safeguarding policy,” RANA stated, adding that Parliament must clarify whether it has existing child protection guidelines for school visits and public engagements involving minors. The group has asked Parliament to publish any existing safeguarding policy, introduce mandatory training for MPs and staff who engage with children, establish reporting mechanisms, and develop clear rules on issues such as photography, privacy and communication with minors. RANA also called on the government to develop minimum child safeguarding standards across public institutions, including ministries, agencies, local assemblies and state programmes involving children. The organisation maintained that while the MP’s apology should be acknowledged, the focus must remain on protecting the child and ensuring institutions create safer environments for children.

items.title: Mandarines : le Maroc s'impose en Irlande et relègue l'Espagne au second plan
items.description: Le Maroc poursuit sa progression sur le marché européen des agrumes. En Irlande, les exportations marocaines de mandarines ont presque doublé en quatre campagnes et dépassent désormais largement celles de l'Espagne. Derrière cette évolution se cachent des choix variétaux, un calendrier de production mieux maîtrisé et une stratégie commerciale qui porte ses fruits. Le Maroc prend l'avantage. L'Irlande confirme la montée en puissance des agrumes marocains. Selon les données du Central Statistics Office analysées par EastFruit, le Royaume a exporté 8.700 tonnes de mandarines entre octobre 2025 et mai 2026, contre un volume espagnol en nette baisse. En quatre ans, les ventes marocaines ont pratiquement doublé tandis que celles de l'Espagne ont reculé d'environ 30 %. Cette évolution s'explique par plusieurs facteurs. Les producteurs marocains ont investi dans des variétés très demandées comme la Nadorcott, la Tango ou la Satsuma, appréciées pour leur facilité d'épluchage et l'absence de pépins. À cela s'ajoute une capacité à prolonger la campagne jusqu'au printemps, permettant d'approvisionner le marché alors que l'offre européenne diminue. Même si ce marché reste modeste comparé à d'autres pays européens, il constitue un bon indicateur des tendances de consommation. Dépourvue de production locale, l'Irlande dépend entièrement des importations. Le fait que les mandarines marocaines représentent jusqu'à 75 % des importations mensuelles pendant certaines périodes montre que le Royaume est devenu un fournisseur de référence. La dynamique observée en Irlande rejoint celle enregistrée au Royaume-Uni, où le Maroc a également renforcé sa présence ces dernières années. Cette progression traduit une stratégie d'exportation qui vise à consolider la place des agrumes marocains sur les marchés d'Europe du Nord. Le défi consiste désormais à maintenir cette avance dans un contexte de concurrence accrue et d'aléas climatiques. Pour les exportateurs marocains, l'enjeu n'est plus seulement de conquérir de nouveaux marchés, mais de conserver les positions acquises face à des concurrents historiques. items.title: ADC expressses commitment to rebuilding party in Rivers
items.description: By Davies Iheamnachor The African Democratic Congress, ADC, has reaffirmed its commitment to rebuilding and strengthening the party in Rivers State. The party also called on members and faithful to embrace peace, unity and respect for the rule of law following the resolution of its leadership dispute by the courts. The factional State Publicity Secretary of the party, Chief Luckyman Egila, in a statement in Port Harcourt said the party was compelled to address what he called a persistent misinformation, falsehood and misrepresentation by individuals allegedly parading themselves as executives of the party at the state, local government and ward level in the face of existing court judgments. Egila explained that the leadership dispute was resolved by the Federal High Court, Abuja Division, in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/581/2026, which nullified the congresses and convention conducted in violation of the party’s constitution. He noted that fresh congresses were subsequently conducted, producing duly elected executives, including the Rivers State leadership. Egila said the current Rivers State Executive Committee is led by State Chairman, Engr. Ode Lawrence Egbagiri, alongside Hon. Iheanyi Eugene Eke as State Secretary, Barr. Hamza Victor Chukure as State Legal Adviser, Chief Luckyman Egila as State Publicity Secretary, Comrade Emmanuel Deinma as State Youth Leader and Hon. Helen Sese Cookey-Gan as State Woman Leader, among other officers elected to serve for a four-year tenure. The ADC further disclosed that the Court of Appeal, Abuja Division, on July 13, 2026, dismissed an appeal challenging the Federal High Court judgment, thereby affirming the legality of the congresses and the leadership that emerged from the new process. He urged the public to disregard any claims or representations made by persons outside the recognised executive committee led by Egbagiri. He maintained that the appellate court’s decision reaffirmed the supremacy of its constitution and underscored the importance of internal democracy, insisting that no individual, regardless of status or influence, is above the constitution of the party. Egila called on its members, stakeholders and supporters across Rivers State to remain calm, law-abiding and united, stressing that the judgment should be seen as an opportunity to heal old divisions, strengthen internal cohesion and reposition the party for greater political relevance. He said: “Our struggle has never been about personalities, titles or positions. It has always been about preserving the sanctity of our Party Constitution, protecting democratic institutions and ensuring that the rule of law prevails over arbitrariness. “The lawful Rivers State Executive Committee remains fully committed to rebuilding, repositioning and strengthening the African Democratic Congress into a formidable political platform founded upon justice, internal democracy, inclusiveness, accountability, transparency and unwavering respect for the rule of law.” The post ADC expressses commitment to rebuilding party in Rivers appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ‘I’m looking forward to sharing the pitch with Rogers’ — Palmer
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Chelsea star Cole Palmer says he is eager to reunite with close friend Morgan Rogers at Stamford Bridge after the England international completed his move from Aston Villa, revealing he “can’t wait” to share the pitch with his former Manchester City academy teammate. Speaking during Chelsea’s pre-season tour in Australia, Palmer told the club’s official website that he played a role in convincing Rogers to join the Blues and believes the pair can rediscover the chemistry they built together in Manchester City’s academy and England’s youth teams. “Everyone knows how good he is, and obviously he’s one of my best friends, so I’m very happy about him coming here,” Palmer said. “We always speak and when I heard Chelsea were trying to sign him, I was texting him even more persuading him to come. He was probably sick of me by that point! I’m glad he’s here now and I’m looking forward to sharing the pitch with him.” Palmer revealed Rogers informed him about the move before it was officially announced, although both players agreed to keep the transfer a secret. “He told me straightaway that he was coming, but we kept it to ourselves. It was a difficult secret to keep before it was announced!” he added. The 24-year-old also backed the new partnership to flourish under manager Xabi Alonso, highlighting how their contrasting styles could benefit Chelsea. “I think we’re different players who can both offer a lot to the team. He’s more physical than me, on and off the ball, and he likes to drive forward more, whereas I think I like to play more passes. “I think we can play well together, and we obviously did that when we were young anyway.” Palmer also joked about Rogers copying his trademark “ice cold” celebration after the winger claimed he had used the gesture before his Chelsea teammate. “I’ve trademarked it so if he tries to do anything, he’ll have bailiffs at his door,” Palmer laughed before adding, “No, we’ll do it together.” Palmer also spoke positively about life under new head coach Xabi Alonso, revealing the Spaniard had reached out to him after he missed England’s World Cup squad and has already outlined how he wants to use him this season. “I spoke to Xabi before he arrived. He messaged me when I didn’t make the World Cup squad. It was nice to hear from him,” Palmer said. “Working under him so far has been really good. Him and his staff have been great, and we’re looking forward to working with him. He says he sees me as a No. 10, playing in the pockets.” Palmer added that he feels refreshed after enjoying his longest off-season in years and is optimistic about Chelsea’s prospects ahead of the new campaign. “I feel good now. I’ve had seven weeks to get myself ready for the season and I’m good to go. I’m looking forward to the season. I had around seven weeks off and I’ve never really had that before. I feel refreshed for the season ahead.” Chelsea continues their pre-season preparations against Tottenham Hotspur in Sydney on Saturday before facing Juventus in Hong Kong. The post ‘I’m looking forward to sharing the pitch with Rogers’ — Palmer appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Accident tragique de bus à Boumerdès : des témoignages glaçants
items.description: Cela devait être une journée de plage, une excursion pour se changer les idées, se baigner, s’amuser et profiter des plaisirs de la mer. En s’installant dans le bus qui les ramenait vers 3 heures du matin, de Sétif à Boumerdès, ces jeunes étaient loin de se douter, que ce véhicule allait se transformer en cercueil. Tragique. Horrible. Choquant. Les premiers arrivés sur les lieux de l’accident témoignent de la violence de l’accident. « Les freins du bus étaient incontrôlable. Ils ont subitement lâché. Le bus a alors heurté la glissière de sécurité, et s’est précipité dans le ravin en faisant des tonneaux. Arrivés sur les lieux, une poignée de secondes après le drame, des citoyens ont été profondément choqués par ce carnage. Une horreur que l’on ne souhaite à personne », raconte un témoin dans une vidéo postée sur les réseaux sociaux. L'horreur sur une route de Boumerdès : des témoins racontent Et il ajoute : « Je veux donner un conseil aux chauffeurs de bus, qui accompagne les estivants à la plage tous les jours, réduisez la vitesse. Cette descente, sur 800 mètres, ne pardonne pas. Ces jeunes sont venus pour aller à la plage, et maintenant ils sont morts. Paix à leurs âmes ! » regrette-t-il. Encore sous le choc, un autre témoin raconte : « Je passais en voiture avec un ami, lorsqu’on a vu un bus débouler à tombeau ouvert. Ce n’était pas une vitesse normale, on aurait dit que les freins avaient lâché. En arrivant au niveau du pont, le bus a commencé à se balancer de gauche à droite. Les gens sotaient par les vitres en agrippant leur sac à dos. Le chauffeur a tenté de stabiliser le bus, mais celui-ci a basculé au fond du ravin. Incapable de regarder cette horrible scène -je suis opéré du cœur-, j’ai baissé les yeux, mais en relevant la tête, j’ai aperçu des gens remonter du complexe en courant, talonnés par des gendarmes ». Moins d’une année après l’accident tragique du bus à Oued El Harrach, voilà qu’un nouveau drame vient endeuiller des familles, en ce dernier jour de juillet. Vitesse ? Véhicule défectueux ? Erreur humaine ? L’enquête de la gendarmerie devrait déterminer les circonstances exactes de ce terrible accident qui a profondément bouleversé les Algériens. Le président Abdelmadjid Tebboune a dit que la justice frappera d'une main de fort contre les responsables éventuels de nouveau carnage routier. L’article Accident tragique de bus à Boumerdès : des témoignages glaçants est apparu en premier sur TSA .

Troops rescue 14 kidnap victims on Lagos-Benin highway
items.description: Troops of the 4 Brigade, Nigerian Army, Benin, have rescued 14 kidnap victims following an operation along the Lagos-Benin Expressway. Capt. Kennedy Anyanwu, Assistant Director, Army Public Relations, 4 Brigade Nigerian Army, disclosed this in a statement made available to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Friday. Anyanwu said the operation, which took place in the Ovia North-East Local Government Area of Edo section of the road, was carried out by troops participating in Operation WABAIZIGAN. The rescue, he said, followed a kidnap incident along the highway on Thursday night. According to him, the troops on routine patrol received credible intelligence on the incident at about 9:30 p.m. and immediately launched a pursuit of the kidnappers along their escape route. “The sustained pressure mounted by the troops forced the kidnappers to abandon 11 abducted victims before fleeing into the surrounding forest. “Troops subsequently launched a follow-up clearance operation in the forest on Friday, leading to the rescue of the remaining three victims. “All 14 rescued victims underwent preliminary debriefing and medical assessment and were confirmed to be in stable condition,” he said. Anyanwu noted that the victims had since been reunited with their families and allowed to continue their journeys. He added that efforts were ongoing to track down and apprehend the fleeing kidnappers. According to him, the operation underscored the army’s operational readiness and intelligence-driven approach to tackling kidnapping and other violent crimes in collaboration with other security agencies. He, however, urged members of the public to continue providing timely and credible information to security agencies to support ongoing operations against criminal elements. Meanwhile, the commander of the 4 Brigade, Brig. -Gen. Ahmed Balogun commended the troops for their professionalism, resilience, and courage during the operation. Balogun reassured residents of Edo and commuters using the Lagos-Benin Expressway of the brigade’s commitment to protecting lives and property. He said troops would sustain aggressive operations to deny criminal elements safe havens and ensure a secure environment for law-abiding citizens. (NAN) The post Troops rescue 14 kidnap victims on Lagos-Benin highway appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Prince Adu-Owusu: The August that changed everything
items.description: There are months we simply pass through, and there are months that quietly become part of who we are. They return every year carrying memories we never asked them to keep. For me, August has become one of those months. Whenever it arrives, I find myself smiling before I become quiet. It reminds me of a season when everything felt possible. A season when one conversation made the future seem clearer than it had ever been. Before I asked her to be my girlfriend, I wanted certainty. Not because I doubted my feelings, but because I respected what love meant. I wasn’t looking for something casual. I wasn’t interested in passing time or filling a space in my life. If I was going to ask someone to walk that journey with me, I wanted to know we were looking in the same direction. So we talked. We spoke about relationships, commitment, expectations, and the kind of future we both hoped to build. We talked about communication, honesty, patience, and the things that make love last long after the excitement of the beginning has settled. Every conversation left me more convinced that she was someone worth taking a chance on. Then August came. With all the courage I could gather, I finally told her how I felt. She didn’t hesitate. She accepted with a sincerity that still stays with me today. It wasn’t simply the word “yes” that touched me. It was everything that came with it. The warmth in her response. The certainty in her words. The hope she gave me without even realizing it. For the first time in a long time, I stopped imagining life as something I would build alone. Her acceptance did something I never expected. It gave me permission to dream. Suddenly, the future didn’t feel like a distant idea anymore. It felt close enough to touch. I found myself imagining ordinary moments that had suddenly become extraordinary. Conversations after long days. Shared prayers before bed. Celebrating milestones together. Growing through life’s challenges as partners rather than strangers. Love has a remarkable way of making tomorrow feel real. Looking back now, I realize that hope is one of the greatest gifts another person can ever give you. Hope changes the way you wake up in the morning. It changes the way you pray. It changes the way you plan your life. And sometimes, all of that begins with one sincere answer. Life, however, has a way of reminding us that not every beautiful beginning becomes a lasting story. Within weeks, something changed. The conversations that once flowed so naturally became shorter. The warmth I had grown used to slowly faded into distance. The certainty that had filled my heart was replaced by questions I couldn’t answer. I searched for reasons without finding many. I held on to hope a little longer because I believed that what we had shared couldn’t disappear so quickly. Eventually, I had to accept that life had chosen a different ending from the one I had imagined. For a long time, I thought August only reminded me of what I lost. But as the years pass, I am beginning to see it differently. August didn’t just teach me that love can end. It taught me that hope is a beautiful thing, even when it doesn’t lead where we expected. I do not regret loving sincerely. I do not regret believing her. I do not regret the dreams I allowed myself to dream. Because if love is ever going to find us, it deserves to be met with courage, not fear. Today, August still feels different. It still carries memories that make me pause. It still reminds me of a young man who believed he had found the person he would spend his life with. But it also reminds me of something else. That every chapter, no matter how short, leaves us with something worth carrying forward. Some chapters leave us with a person. Others leave us with a lesson. August gave me both. And perhaps that is why it will always be the month that changed everything. ********* The writer is an online journalist and a freelance graphic designer with The Multimedia Group. Email: prince.adu-owusu@myjoyonline.com and Linkedin@ https://www.linkedin.com/in/prince-adu-owusu/

items.title: Ato Forson announces ‘New Economy’ policy for 2027 budget, promises shift to growth-focused spending
items.description: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has announced plans to introduce a new policy framework dubbed the “New Economy” in the 2027 national budget, signalling a shift from fiscal consolidation towards growth-focused spending. Speaking on JoyNews’ PM Express programme during “The Mid-Year Scorecard: One-on-One with the Finance Minister” with Evans Mensah, Dr Forson said the government’s initial two years in office were focused on difficult economic decisions aimed at stabilising the economy. He said the 2027 budget would mark a new phase of recovery focused on expanding economic opportunities, particularly in the rural sector and among young people. “The 2027 budget, I’m going to announce a new policy called the new economy,” he said. According to the Finance Minister, the government deliberately undertook a two-year adjustment period, but intends to ease the pace of fiscal consolidation as the economy improves. “I have always known that we will need that two years of hard decisions to turn around this economy. We have. I don’t want to celebrate too early. I want to wait till the end of the year and launch the new economy for 2027,” he stated. Dr Forson explained that government intends to reduce its primary surplus target from 1.5% of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) to 0.5% of GDP, describing the move as a one percentage point relaxation of the adjustment programme. “So simple put, I’m going to relax the adjustment by one percentage point of GDP. It means you have one percentage more to spend on the new economy,” he said. He said the additional fiscal space would be directed towards sectors expected to stimulate growth and improve livelihoods. “We are going to target the rural sector of this economy. Market women who you met. For growth. For young people and for growth,” he added. The Finance Minister said the government’s focus would be on policies that directly impact citizens while supporting broader economic transformation. “I don’t want to read the 2027 budget I have. But I can assure you that we will focus on the people and turn around this economy at scale and transform it,” he said. Dr Forson added that the planned approach reflects President John Dramani Mahama’s economic vision, with his role being to support its implementation. “That is the vision of His Excellency President Mahama. And that is my job to assist him deliver,” he stated. The announcement comes ahead of the presentation of the 2027 budget, which is expected to outline government’s next phase of economic policy after its current fiscal adjustment programme.

items.title: Détention, transport et importation de drogue à haut risque : deux Guinéens, un Portugais et deux Nigérians condamnés à de lourdes peines par le TPI de Kaloum
items.description: Le tribunal criminel de Kaloum a condamné, ce vendredi 31 juillet 2026, cinq narcotrafiquants de nationalités guinéenne, portugaise et nigériane à de lourdes peines allant de cinq à dix ans de réclusion criminelle. Il s’agit de Mohamed Thiam, Mamadou Yero Sylla (en fuite), Bernardo Da Silva, Linus Obunajike et Destiny Chijioke, tous poursuivis pour des faits de détention, transport et importation de drogue à haut risque. Ils étaient en détention depuis décembre 2024, à l’exception de Mamadou Yero Sylla, en fuite. Selon le tribunal, les accusés ont été interpellés à bord d’un navire naviguant dans les eaux territoriales guinéennes, où les services compétents avaient découvert 20 colis contenant 600 kilogrammes de cocaïne. Dans son verdict rendu ce vendredi, le tribunal a condamné les quatre accusés présents à l’audience, à savoir Mohamed Thiam, Bernardo Da Silva, Linus Obunajike et Destiny Chijioke, à cinq ans de réclusion criminelle. Ils ont également été condamnés solidairement au paiement de 200 millions de francs guinéens de dommages et intérêts. Le tribunal a en outre ordonné la confiscation du navire au profit de l’État, ainsi que la confiscation et l’incinération des 600 kilogrammes de cocaïne saisis. Les ressortissants étrangers Bernardo Da Silva, Linus Obunajike et Destiny Chijioke ont également été interdits de séjour sur le territoire guinéen pendant huit ans après l’exécution de leur peine. Quant à Mamadou Yéro Sylla, toujours en fuite, il a été reconnu coupable de complicité. Il a été condamné à 10 ans de réclusion criminelle, et un mandat d’arrêt a été décerné à son encontre. Elisa CAMARA L’article Détention, transport et importation de drogue à haut risque : deux Guinéens, un Portugais et deux Nigérians condamnés à de lourdes peines par le TPI de Kaloum est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Kidnapping: Make Oriire rescue the standard, not the exception, ADC tells Tinubu
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja The African Democratic Congress, ADC, on Friday urged President Bola Tinubu to make the successful rescue of abducted pupils and teachers in Oriire Local Government Area of Oyo State the national benchmark for fighting kidnapping, insisting that every Nigerian held captive, regardless of where they live, deserves the same urgency and determination from the Federal Government. The opposition party said the rescue had given hope to many Nigerians but also left grieving families with an unavoidable question: if the government could free the Oriire victims without yielding to kidnappers’ demands, why should families in Kwara, Borno, and other states still be waiting for the same hope? In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC welcomed the rescue operation but urged the Tinubu administration to extend the same resolve nationwide. Abdullahi was reacting to the president’s remarks on Thursday while receiving traditional rulers from Oyo State, led by the Olubadan of Ibadanland, at the Presidential Villa, Abuja, where Tinubu disclosed that his administration rejected negotiations with the kidnappers and instead relied on security operations, including targeting the kidnappers’ families. “The rescue in Oriire should not stand as an exceptional story that the government recounts with pride. It should be the standard by which every response to kidnapping is measured,” the ADC said. The party said every life rescued from kidnappers was a victory for the country and every reunited family a source of relief but stressed that the true measure of effective governance was whether such outcomes became routine rather than exceptional. “Those families ask for no special treatment. They ask only for equal humanity and equal citizenship,” Abdullahi added. The ADC said hundreds of families in Kwara State still wake each day uncertain whether abducted relatives are alive, while communities in Borno, Zamfara, Kaduna, Niger, Benue, and other parts of the country continue to wait for loved ones who have remained in captivity. “If the Federal Government has the intelligence network, the operational capacity, and the political resolve to bring the victims in Oriire home without yielding to the demands of kidnappers, why has the government not applied the same strategy to rescue other victims who have fallen victims much longer and have continued to languish in kidnappers’ dens till today?” the party asked. The party argued that the president’s account of the Oriire operation demonstrated that the government possessed the capability to confront kidnappers decisively and should apply that determination wherever Nigerians are abducted, irrespective of geography or ethnicity. According to the ADC, “The president told the kidnappers in Oriire, ‘No deal.’ He must demonstrate equal resolve and send an equally unmistakable message and give real hope to families still waiting for a son, daughter, husband, wife, or parent that the government has not forgotten them.” The opposition party maintained that the true test of any administration was not success in a single operation but its ability to build a system that prevents kidnappings and assures citizens that rescue efforts will not depend on where an abduction occurs. It urged the Federal Government to deploy the same intelligence, surveillance, and operational determination that secured the Oriire rescue in every state where Nigerians remain in captivity. “No family should have to wonder whether the urgency of government depends on where tragedy happens,” the ADC said. items.title: Affaire « Dolo » et incivisme à bord d’un bus : Les passagers indélicats condamnés à laver les véhicules de la SOTRACO et à curer des caniveaux
items.description: Ce qui ne devait être qu’une simple virée festive entre amis s'est transformé en une leçon de civisme nationale. Après la diffusion virale d'images montrant des passagers consommant du « dolo » et adoptant des comportements inappropriés à bord d'un bus de la SOTRACO le 18 juillet 2026, la réaction des autorités à travers la Brigade Laabal ne s'est pas fait attendre. Au-delà du rappel à l'ordre institutionnel, les auteurs de ces actes ont été interceptés et condamnés à des travaux d'intérêt commun. Entre nettoyage de bus et curage de caniveaux, la sanction se veut pédagogique pour rappeler que, même dans le cadre d’une location privée, le respect du bien public reste une obligation citoyenne absolue. La vidéo, partagée des milliers de fois le week-end dernier, a suscité une vive indignation au sein de l'opinion publique burkinabè. On y voyait des passagers en pleine réjouissance, bouteilles de dolo à la main, transformant l'intérieur d'un bus vert et jaune en véritable zone de non-droit. L'incident, survenu lors d'un déplacement privé vers Boussouma, a déclenché une riposte immédiate de la Direction Générale de la SOTRACO et des autorités de régulation sociale. Dans une mise au point ferme, le Directeur Général de la SOTRACO, Drissa Sawadogo, a précisé que si le bus faisait l'objet d'un affrètement privé, cela ne soustrayait en rien les usagers aux règles élémentaires de décence. « L'intérieur des bus, dès la montée à bord, devient systématiquement un espace public », rappellent les sources. L'introduction d'alcool, la production de déchets et les propos malsains y sont formellement proscrits pour garantir la sécurité et la préservation du matériel national. L'offensive ne s'est pas limitée à des communiqués. Les auteurs des actes de vandalisme et d'incivisme vus dans la vidéo ont été interceptés par la Brigade Laabal. La sanction est tombée, immédiate et symbolique : ils sont désormais soumis à des travaux d'intérêt commun. Leur peine consistera à laver les bus de la SOTRACO chaque jour pendant une période indéterminée, ainsi qu'à participer à des travaux de pavage et de curage de caniveaux. Cette intervention s'inscrit dans la mission de la Brigade Laal, véritable instrument civique au service de la refondation nationale. Au-delà de la morale, c'est la sécurité des usagers qui est mise en avant. La consommation d'alcool et les comportements bruyants créent des « éclats de voix » qui distraient le conducteur et augmentent considérablement les risques d'accident. Pour la SOTRACO, il s'agit de protéger tant le climat social à bord que la vie des passagers. Face à ces dérives, un appel au sursaut patriotique est lancé. Le transport public doit redevenir une « fierté nationale » où la discipline est l'affaire de tous. Le respect envers les conducteurs, les contrôleurs, et la priorité accordée aux personnes âgées ou à mobilité réduite sont érigés en devoirs moraux. Désormais, tout manquement constaté par les agents d'exploitation entraînera l'arrêt immédiat du service, signifiant que le « dolo » n'a plus sa place sur les routes de la SOTRACO. L’article Affaire « Dolo » et incivisme à bord d’un bus : Les passagers indélicats condamnés à laver les véhicules de la SOTRACO et à curer des caniveaux est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Burkina/Apurement du passif social: plus de 16 000 agents de santé ont perçu leurs droits
items.description: Quatre mois après le lancement de l'opération d'apurement du passif social de l'Agence nationale de gestion des soins de santé primaires (AGSP), les résultats affichés sont encourageants. Plus de 16 000 agents de santé ont déjà perçu leurs droits, pour un montant dépassant 25,6 milliards de FCFA, soit plus de 72 % de l'enveloppe prévue. L'information a été donnée, ce vendredi 31 juillet 2026, au cours d'une conférence de presse, présidée par le premier responsable de l'AGSP, Dékwinzou Frédéric Loué. L'Agence nationale de gestion des soins de santé primaires (AGSP) poursuit l'exécution de son programme d'apurement du passif social de ses agents. À l'occasion d'un point de presse tenu, ce vendredi 31 juillet 2026 à Ouagadougou, le directeur général de l'institution, Dékwinzou Frédéric Loué, a présenté les résultats enregistrés à mi-parcours de cette opération engagée par le gouvernement. Lancée en avril dernier et prévue pour s'achever en octobre 2026, cette initiative vise à régulariser la situation administrative et financière de 18 455 agents de santé, tout en consolidant les relations de confiance entre l'administration et son personnel. Pour atteindre cet objectif, une enveloppe globale de 35,42 milliards de FCFA a été mobilisée. Selon les chiffres communiqués, à la date du 25 juillet 2026, 16 096 agents avaient déjà bénéficié du règlement de leurs droits, pour un montant total de 25 679 893 430 F CFA, correspondant à un taux d'exécution financière de 72,49 %. Ces paiements couvrent plusieurs droits liés à la carrière des agents, notamment les avancements, les reversements, les reclassements ainsi que diverses indemnités prévues par les textes en vigueur. Des hommes et femmes de médias présents à la conférence de l'AGSP «Les résultats obtenus en seulement quatre mois traduisent la volonté des autorités de rétablir les agents de santé dans leurs droits et de renforcer la confiance entre l'administration et les travailleurs», a indiqué le directeur général de l'AGSP, Dékwinzou Frédéric Loué. Parallèlement aux paiements, des avancées significatives ont également été réalisées dans le traitement des dossiers administratifs. Sur les 18 117 décisions d'avancement attendues, 17 494 ont déjà été élaborées, soit un taux d'exécution de 96,56 %. Les opérations relatives aux décisions de reversement ainsi qu'aux certificats de cessation de paiement connaissent également une progression jugée satisfaisante par les responsables de l'institution. Afin d'éviter la reconstitution de nouveaux arriérés, le ministère de la Santé a engagé plusieurs réformes structurelles. Celles-ci portent notamment sur l'assainissement du fichier de paie de l'AGSP, la digitalisation de la programmation des activités à travers la plateforme SYSPROG, l'amélioration de la gestion des actes administratifs de carrière, le renforcement des compétences des responsables des ressources humaines des districts sanitaires et des directions régionales de la santé, ainsi que la mise en place de codes de traitement propres à chaque district sanitaire. «Notre ambition est non seulement d'apurer définitivement le passif social, mais aussi de mettre en place des mécanismes durables afin que les droits des agents soient désormais traités avec davantage de célérité et de transparence», a souligné Dékwinzou Frédéric Loué. Avec un peu plus de deux mois avant la fin de l'opération, l'AGSP affiche sa détermination à achever l'apurement du passif social dans les délais fixés. Les réformes engagées devraient, selon les autorités, contribuer à moderniser durablement la gestion des ressources humaines du secteur de la santé et à prévenir l'accumulation de nouveaux arriérés. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Burkina/Apurement du passif social: plus de 16 000 agents de santé ont perçu leurs droits est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Schengen’s Greatest Failure
items.description: I n the summer of 1985 , representatives from five Western European countries met aboard a riverboat in Schengen, a wine-making village in Luxembourg, to celebrate the removal of checkpoints at their borders. According to the treaty they approved, which became known as the Schengen Agreement, the signatory countries sought “solidarity between their peoples by removing obstacles to free movement,” forming a borderless zone that gave tangible expression to principles of liberal internationalism that were ascendant as the West glimpsed victory in the Cold War. Schengen has succeeded spectacularly, at least by certain metrics. It has grown to include 29 countries, from Portugal to Poland, and more than 450 million people. Four decades on, it remains one of Europe’s most popular policies among people who benefit from it—those who work, study, shop, date, and live across borders, able to cross multiple European states in a matter of hours, without ever stopping their car. But as a mechanism to build European solidarity, Schengen has been a failure. The latest evidence of that came this week, when as many as 60,000 migrants from Morocco rushed into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta, which sits on the North African coast of the Mediterranean. Ceuta has a population of only 83,000 and isn’t even on the European continent. But because it is part of Spain, entering Ceuta, in theory, affords access to 29 countries. The migrants swam or climbed over fences to reach the tiny territory. Several dozen have died. Spain’s prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, decried the situation as an “attack” and a violation of his country’s territorial integrity, vowing that the migrants would be turned back; according to Spain’s interior ministry, more than half of them already have been. Sánchez blamed trafficking gangs, and others pointed a finger at Moroccan authorities for possibly instigating or enabling the huge number of crossings into the Schengen Area, dwarfing equivalent single-day figures from the European migration crisis in 2015. Morocco’s ambassador to Spain disputed such allegations. [ Rogé Karma: The Spanish exception ] The political blowback for Sánchez, a leftist whose pro-immigrant position has differentiated him in an era of resurgent nationalism, was predictable. Criticism came from his domestic opposition in Madrid, as well as from the White House, where President Trump saw an opportunity to paint Europe as lax on immigration and identify an edge for his party as the midterms approach. “That’s going to be us in three years if the wrong side gets in,” Trump told Fox News. The most notable reactions, however, came from other European capitals, which once committed themselves to freedom of movement as a basis for cross-border solidarity, an integral part of shared European Union membership that also includes a common trade policy and, in most cases, a shared currency. Giorgia Meloni, the right-wing prime minister of Italy, called for the suspension of Spain’s Schengen membership (for which there is no formal process), and her foreign minister blamed the Spanish government for the chaos, labeling its plans to grant legal status to more than half a million migrants “profoundly wrong.” In response, Madrid summoned the Italian ambassador, accusing foreign leaders of “partisan demagoguery.” Other countries backed Meloni. Finland’s interior minister argued that Spain had “completely failed to protect the Schengen Area’s external border from infiltration,” adding in a post on social media, “This cannot continue.” France increased checks at its border with Spain, and the chancellor of Austria, which is about 1,000 miles from the Iberian Peninsula, said his country was weighing whether to close its borders. T here is no evidence that any of the new arrivals in Ceuta have crossed the Strait of Gibraltar to the Spanish mainland. Transiting the strait typically requires a ferry or plane, and involves border and identity checks that validate whether passengers have the relevant visas. Meanwhile, there aren’t legal mechanisms to suspend a country’s Schengen membership, especially unilaterally. What other countries can do is reintroduce controls at their borders. The authority to do so was written into an implementing convention approved by the signatory states in 1990, and they’ve made liberal use of it. Italy had already reimposed checks at its land border with France because of the anticipated presence of “radical activists” at a festival in Piedmont, in northwestern Italy, and earlier today, Meloni’s government halted passport-free travel at air and sea borders with Spain. Austria had already reintroduced controls at borders with four of its neighbors, citing irregular migration through the Balkans, the burden of migrants on its asylum system, and the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East. But these piecemeal steps to police borders aren’t grandiose enough when there’s political hay to be made of immigration. Meloni can’t be outdone by her deputy prime minister and coalition partner, Matteo Salvini, who has taken to social media in recent days to urge, vaguely yet repeatedly, “Suspend Schengen.” Marine Le Pen, the far-right firebrand in France and a candidate for president in next year’s elections, vowed today to restrict the agreement if she came to power. Le Pen’s party, now called National Rally, has expertly channeled anger about Schengen. Amid the 2015 refugee crisis, when more than 1 million people crossed into Europe, mostly in flight from the Syrian civil war, party representatives performed death rites on the riverbank near where the agreement was signed 30 years earlier. They laid a funereal wreath on a star-etched monument to the system of free movement created there. [ Read: Europe’s far right is turning on Trump ] The corps of mid-level diplomats who created Schengen gave little consideration to its political consequences. “We did our job as junior ministers,” the French representative, Catherine Lalumière, told me as part of research for my book on the history of the agreement . They thought that borderless travel would fulfill promises made by the Treaty of Rome, the founding document of European integration, and advance both the development of a common market and the cultivation of solidarity among member states. By no means did they anticipate incendiary debates over immigration. Except there were signs of a potent backlash already at that time. In 1983, the National Front, as Le Pen’s far-right party was then known, came to power for the first time in French municipal elections, in a small town called Dreux. A year after Schengen’s creation, the party entered the national Parliament for the first time, in elections held in 1986. As anti-immigrant populism gained influence in France, the government in Paris helped lead the drafting of Schengen’s implementing convention, trying to pair internal freedom of movement with security at Europe’s external borders. Language about “solidarity” present in the original agreement was nowhere to be found in the 1990 document. Instead, more than half of the convention’s 142 articles dealt with security and the exchange of data necessary to crack down on unwanted immigration of the kind now seen in Spain’s offshore exclave. The crisis in Ceuta is likely to be contained, and quickly. But if Europe’s reaction to a surge of immigration is to isolate individual states, rather than to use the tools it created to protect freedom and manage human displacement in a globalized world, Schengen really is at risk.

items.title: Soumba–Tanènè : le ministre des Infrastructures engage des mesures d’urgence pour rétablir la circulation sur cet axe stratégique fortement dégradé
items.description: Le ministre des Infrastructures, M. Facinet Sylla, s'est rendu, ce vendredi 31 juillet 2026, sur le tronçon Soumba–Tanènè afin de constater de visu l'état de dégradation de cette route, l'un des principaux corridors de transport du pays et un axe essentiel pour l'économie nationale. Cette visite intervient à la suite d'une première mission technique dépêchée par le ministère pour évaluer les dommages constatés et proposer des solutions immédiates en attendant une réhabilitation complète. Face à l'urgence de la situation, le ministre a ordonné le déploiement de cinq entreprises nationales afin d'engager sans délai des travaux d'urgence sur les sections les plus critiques de la route. « Cette visite de terrain fait suite à une première mission technique que j'avais dépêchée afin d'évaluer les dégradations observées et de proposer des mesures d'urgence pour rétablir la praticabilité de cet axe. Avant même ma venue aujourd'hui, j'ai demandé à AGEROUTE et aux autres services de mon département de mobiliser, dans les meilleurs délais, cinq entreprises citoyennes pour intervenir sur les points les plus critiques du tronçon et permettre le maintien de la circulation », a déclaré le ministre Facinet Sylla. Depuis environ quatre ans, le chantier de réhabilitation de ce tronçon accuse un retard, principalement en raison des difficultés liées au règlement des factures des entreprises contractantes. Cette situation a favorisé une dégradation accélérée de la chaussée, aggravée par le trafic particulièrement intense de poids lourds. Le ministre a rappelé que cette route supporte quotidiennement un volume exceptionnel d'engins. « Nous sommes sur l'une des routes les plus sollicitées, sinon la plus sollicitée du pays. Elle accueille quotidiennement des véhicules miniers ainsi que des camions transportant des matériaux de construction. À cela s'ajoute le problème récurrent des surcharges qui, quelle que soit la qualité de la route que nous réaliserons ici, entraîneront une dégradation rapide si elles ne sont pas maîtrisées », a-t-il expliqué. Pour préserver durablement les investissements de l'État, le ministre des Infrastructures a annoncé l'installation prochaine d'un dispositif de pesage des essieux sur le nouvel aménagement. Cet équipement permettra de contrôler avec précision le poids des véhicules lourds et de lutter efficacement contre les surcharges, identifiées comme l'une des principales causes de la détérioration prématurée des infrastructures routières. Il a également annoncé la réhabilitation complète de cet axe stratégique dès la fin de la saison des pluies, afin de doter les populations d'une infrastructure moderne, sûre et durable. Sur le terrain, les premières interventions sont déjà visibles. Les engins sont mobilisés et les travaux se concentrent sur le reprofilage de la chaussée ainsi que le traitement des points les plus dégradés. Karim Sy, conducteur des travaux de l'entreprise IC Transport, l'une des cinq sociétés mobilisées, a détaillé les opérations en cours : « Nous intervenons sur un linéaire de plus de 11 kilomètres. Tous les moyens nécessaires ont été mobilisés pour atteindre les objectifs fixés. Nos équipes réalisent le reprofilage de la chaussée et le bouchage des nids-de-poule afin d'assurer la praticabilité de la route pendant cette saison des pluies. Techniquement, nous utilisons des moellons, des matériaux de jointoiement et procédons à un compactage rigoureux pour garantir la stabilité des réparations. » Cette visite traduit la volonté du Gouvernement d'améliorer les conditions de circulation et de préserver le patrimoine routier national. L’article Soumba–Tanènè : le ministre des Infrastructures engage des mesures d'urgence pour rétablir la circulation sur cet axe stratégique fortement dégradé est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: ‘Most difficult period of my career’ — Mudryk reacts after CAS doping ruling
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk has described the last 20 months as “the most difficult period” of his career after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) cleared him to resume playing with immediate effect, bringing an end to his long-running anti-doping case. The 25-year-old made the remarks in a statement shared on his Instagram handle after CAS partially upheld his appeal against a four-year ban, allowing him to return to competitive football. The ruling followed an agreement between Mudryk, the Football Association, and the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA). Earlier on Friday, the BBC reported that Chelsea are set to reintegrate the Ukraine international into the squad, with the winger expected to join the club’s pre-season tour. “This has been the most difficult period of my career,” Mudryk wrote. He added: “I am grateful that this process has reached a conclusion, that I have been cleared to return to football and that I can now look ahead to my future.” Mudryk reiterated that he never knowingly or intentionally took a banned substance, insisting he had maintained that position from the beginning of the case. “As I have always maintained from the outset of this case, I have never knowingly or intentionally taken any banned substance. My commitment to competing fairly and representing my club and country with professionalism and integrity has always been important to me.” The Ukrainian international thanked his family, friends, Chelsea, his teammates, supporters and legal team for standing by him throughout the ordeal. “My focus now is on returning to football, working hard every day, and making a positive contribution on the pitch,” he said. Mudryk has not featured in a competitive match since November 2024 after being provisionally suspended following an adverse finding for meldonium during an out-of-competition test while on international duty with Ukraine. CAS ruled that changes to WADA’s technical reporting standards mean the low concentration of meldonium found in Mudryk’s sample would not have been reported if the test had been conducted under the current guidelines. As part of the settlement, the winger accepted a suspension equivalent to the period already served, making him immediately eligible to return. Chelsea welcomed the decision, saying they now look forward to helping Mudryk regain full fitness and resume his career with the first team. The post ‘Most difficult period of my career’ — Mudryk reacts after CAS doping ruling appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Pas de Patriot made in Ukraine ? «Nous devons faire très attention avant de laisser quiconque en fabriquer», estime Trump
items.description: « Ces armes sont formidables. Nous devons faire tres attention avant de laisser quiconque en fabriquer », a declare Donald Trump ce 31 juillet lors d'une conference de presse a Camp David, apres avoir evoque les batteries sol-air Patriot. Le president des etats-Unis etait alors interroge sur d'autres de ses declarations, parues la veille dans le Financial Times (FT), ou il assurait n'etre « pas sûr » de donner son feu vert a Kiev pour fabriquer localement ces armements. Il renvoyait ainsi a ses declarations du mois passe, selon lesquelles les constructeurs automobiles americains allaient reconvertir certaines de leurs usines afin d'assembler des armes, notamment des missiles de croisiere Tomahawk ainsi que ceux pour les systemes Patriot. « Nous n'avons pas donne notre accord » « Il faut etre tres judicieux et tres prudent aussi. Maintenant, nous n'avons pas donne notre accord », a encore declare Trump. « Nous en discutons. Mais il est difficile de ceder ce genre de technologie. Je ne pense pas que cela arrivera un jour. Mais ceux a qui vous confiez cette technologie pourraient un jour se retourner contre vous », a-t-il ajoute. Depuis plusieurs jours, les rumeurs vont bon train, notamment depuis un reportage de la chaîne allemande Welt evoquant un potentiel refus de Boeing d'octroyer a des pays tiers des licences de production. Ce mastodonte du complexe militaro-industriel etats-unien produit notamment le systeme de guidage des missiles PAC-3, tires par les batteries antiaeriennes MIM-104 Patriot de Raytheon. En marge du sommet annuel de l'OTAN a Ankara, Donald Trump avait promis a Volodymyr Zelensky qu'il allait autoriser Kiev a produire sous licence des missiles Patriot. « Comme ca, vous ne pourrez plus vous plaindre qu'on ne vous en donne pas assez », avait-il lâche a l'attention de Zelensky, deja devant des journalistes, avant d'ajouter : « nous n'en avons pas encore informe l'entreprise, mais ca va s'arranger ».
