items.title: Police nationale: Le Contrôleur Général Missa MILLOGO repose désormais dans son village natal à Oualana, commune de Léna dans la province du Houët
items.description: Ce vendredi 31 juillet 2026, une forte délégation de la haute hiérarchie policière, d'autorités administratives, militaires et paramilitaires, coutumières et religieuses ainsi que des collègues, frères d'armes, parents, amis et connaissances ont rendu un dernier vibrant hommage au Contrôleur Général de Police Missa MILLOGO, précédemment Directeur de la Police Judiciaire (DPJ) de la Direction Générale de la Police Nationale (DGPN). Ce dernier acte plein d'émotions vient clore des obsèques qui, débutées le jeudi 30 juillet 2026 à Ouagadougou, ont été empreintes de récits et de témoignages émouvants, de moments de recueillement, d'hommages et de décoration, tant son parcours a été aussi bien exceptionnel qu'inspirant. En effet, le Contrôleur Général MILLOGO, après avoir décroché sa Maîtrise en Biologie/Microbiologie en 2004 à l'Université de Ouagadougou, décida d’embrasser le métier de Policier qu'il décroche en 2005 et, après deux ans passés à l'Ecole Nationale de Police (ENP), il en ressort en tant que Commissaire de Police. Dès lors, il va se jeter dans une quête permanente de recherche du savoir qu'il aimait tant tout en continuant parallèlement une ascension fulgurante dans son métier d'origine. Ce qui fait que dès 2022, il décrocha sa Thèse de Doctorat Unique (PhD) à l'Université Joseph KI Zerbo et, en 2024, il est fait Chevalier de l'Ordre de l'Etalon pour son abnégation au service de la Nation. En dix (19) ans et demi de bons et loyaux services, le Contrôleur Général MILLOGO aura occupé plusieurs postes et responsabilités parmi lesquels : Commissaire Central Adjoint de Police de la ville de Manga, Directeur de la Police Technique et Scientifique (DPTS), Conseiller Technique du Ministre en charge du Développement Industriel et Directeur de la Police Judiciaire. Expert agréé et consultant avec à son actif plusieurs travaux d'expertise et d'étude réalisés notamment dans les domaines de la sécurité/sûreté ainsi qu'en criminologie et criminalistique, il totalise également plus d'une dizaine d'années de partage de ses connaissances professionnelles et académiques à des apprenants d'universités (Nazi Boni et Thomas Sankara) et d'écoles (ENP, Académie de Police, ENAM). Le Général MILLOGO nous a été arraché le mardi 28 juillet dernier des suites de blessures dues à un accident de la circulation routière. Puisse la terre libre du pays des Hommes intègres être légère pour l'âme du défunt ! Union de Prière ! items.title: ‘How Ed Sheeran helped me land World Cup Song’ — Burna Boy
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Grammy-winning Nigerian singer Burna Boy has revealed that British pop star Ed Sheeran played a key role in his feature with Shakira on the official 2026 FIFA World Cup anthem, Dai Dai. Speaking during a recent interview with Capital FM, the singer narrated how Ed Sheeran called him to work on the World Cup song, noting his earlier anticipation to work with Shakira as a source of motivation. “He’s actually the first to call me about this because he’s the one who had my number. He hit me up and said we should a World cup song with Shakira and I said I’ll love to work with Shakira, let’s do it,” Burna Boy said. The Afrofusion star also disclosed that Sheeran prepared him for the pressure of performing at the 2026 FIFA World Cup final, saying the British singer gave him an early warning about the scale of the event. He added: “He had to give me a heads-up like, ‘Yo, you’re going to have to perform at the finals and all of that.’ He knows me… he knows how I get down. “He knows the stress part is a bit crazy for me, so he gave me a heads-up. He was like, ‘Yo, it’s going to be real stressful.'” Burna Boy described Sheeran as one of the most thoughtful people he has worked with, praising his personality and professionalism. “He’s just a very sensible and lovable guy. He is someone I have taken to personally from the beginning. Ed is very smart, man. He always knows what he is doing.” View this post on Instagram Sheeran is credited as one of the songwriters on Dai Dai, alongside producer Alexander Castillo. Recall Shakira revealed that she waited 20 days for Burna Boy to submit his verse for the World Cup anthem, admitting she was determined to have the Nigerian superstar on the record. The Colombian singer also described Burna Boy’s contribution as the “cherry on top”, saying his vocals elevated the song to “another level”. Released as the official anthem for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, Dai Dai celebrates resilience, unity and inner strength, bringing together two global music stars for one of football’s biggest stages. items.title: Govt cuts petrol price by 12 paisas, diesel by 66 paisas for the next three days
items.description: Pakistan fuel prices, 2026 Official ex-depot prices (PKR/litre) — OGRA & Ministry of Energy notifications Petrol (MS-92) Diesel (HSD) Pre-crisis baseline Source: OGRA / Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division); Dawn.com · "> The government on Friday reduced the prices of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by 12 paisas and 66 paisas per litre, respectively. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs336.03 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs392.38 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs110 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs96 per litre on diesel. The Petroleum Division’s notification said that the new prices would be applicable from August 1 to August 3. Meanwhile, in a bigger price shock, the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) notified a record 32pc increase in the price of regasified liquefied natural gas (RLNG) for August, taking it to $25.83 per mmBtu for SNGPL and $25.09 per mmBtu for SSGCL. This will translate into a retail price of Rs7,204 per mmBtu. The price is based on five imported cargoes from the spot market, as no shipment could be secured from Qatar because of the US-Iran war. This is the single biggest jump in RLNG rates in its decade-long history. This comes on top of an about 15pc increase in the RLNG price fixed last month at $19.52 per mmBtu (Rs5,446 per mmBtu) for SNGPL and $18.63 per mmBtu for SSGCL. Compared with $10.45 (Rs2,916) per mmBtu in February this year, the RLNG price hike works out to around 148pc for August. This mainly results in a substantial increase in fuel costs for power generation. This can be seen from the fact that the fuel cost for RLNG-based power generation in May worked out to Rs31 per unit, compared with Rs13.72 per unit in April. The diesel price has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan this week. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: Migration à Sebta : flux hétérogène et rapatriement total
items.description: Le littoral nord du Royaume vit au rythme d'une urgence migratoire absolue. Ces derniers jours, les tentatives d'entrée illégale dans le préside occupé de Sebta ont pris une ampleur inédite, caractérisée par une hétérogénéité marquante des profils. Loin des vagues migratoires traditionnelles, les traversées à la nage mobilisent désormais une population plurielle : des adolescents, des jeunes adultes, mais aussi des femmes et des noyaux familiaux entiers qui convergent vers l'enclave. Face à cette situation critique, les canaux diplomatiques et sécuritaires des deux pays se sont immédiatement activés pour acter une riposte ferme. Rabat et Madrid ont en effet scellé un accord stipulant le retour et le rapatriement systématique de l’ensemble des migrants ayant réussi à rejoindre la ville occupée au cours des derniers jours. Preuve de la rigueur de ce protocole exceptionnel, cette mesure de reconduite s’appliquera également aux mineurs, sans exception. © Mounir Mehimdate L’opération de reconduite s’effectuera dans le cadre d’une coordination bilatérale étroite entre les deux pays pour désamorcer l’engorgement des infrastructures de transit. Cette crise logistique et humaine sans précédent a d'ailleurs poussé le président du gouvernement local de Sebta, Juan Jesús Vivas, à déclarer une « urgence humanitaire et sociale absolue ». Coordination exemplaire face à l'instrumentalisation des mafias En visite dans le préside ce vendredi 31 juillet, le Premier ministre espagnol, Pedro Sánchez, a apporté un éclairage politique majeur sur les ressorts de ce rush hétérogène. Le chef du gouvernement espagnol a directement incriminé les « mafias de trafiquants d’êtres humains » , les accusant d'avoir propagé une « lecture intéressée » et malhonnête d’un récent arrêt de la Cour suprême statuant sur l'impossibilité théorique de reconduire à la frontière les personnes arrivées par la mer. « Ce qui ressort des échanges que nous avons eus avec les autorités marocaines, c’est une lecture intéressée que les mafias de trafiquants d’êtres humains ont faite d’un arrêt de la Cour suprême » espagnole, a-t-il dit. El Gobierno de España está volcado en dar una respuesta inmediata a la situación en Ceuta. Estamos movilizando todos los recursos necesarios, trabajando con las autoridades marroquíes e internacionales, y preparando las medidas necesarias para recuperar la normalidad lo antes… — Pedro Sánchez (@sanchezcastejon) July 30, 2026 Répandue « comme une traînée de poudre » ces dernières heures, cette fausse interprétation a servi d'appât pour inciter des milliers de profils divers à se jeter à l'eau. Sánchez a fermement qualifié cette vague massive d’ « attaque » et de « violation de l’intégrité territoriale de l’Espagne». © Mounir Mehimdate Sur le terrain, la tension s'est également traduite par des interventions fermes en amont. Ce vendredi matin, la police marocaine a interpellé environ trente jeunes à Fnideq après des heurts à proximité de la frontière, où les forces de l'ordre ont dû utiliser des gaz lacrymogènes et des lances à eau pour disperser un rassemblement massif de plusieurs milliers de personnes qui s'étaient agglomérées ces derniers jours. © Mounir Mehimdate Le Maroc et l'Espagne, dont la coopération en matière de gestion migratoire reste qualifiée d'«exemplaire » , se sont engagés à réviser et exécuter les procédures de refoulement dans les plus brefs délais, dans un objectif commun de faire respecter la souveraineté frontalière et neutraliser les réseaux criminels qui exploitent la détresse sociale pour orchestrer ces flux massifs. The post Migration à Sebta : flux hétérogène et rapatriement total appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Caravane de chirurgie de la cataracte au profit de 595 bénéficiaires à Al Haouz
items.description: Quelque 595 personnes ont bénéficié récemment d'interventions chirurgicales de la cataracte à l'hôpital de proximité d'Aït Ourir (province d'Al Haouz), dans le cadre d'une campagne médicale spécialisée de dépistage et de traitement des maladies oculaires. Organisée pendant 18 jours (du 11 au 29 juillet), cette campagne a été initiée par la Fondation Al Basar, en partenariat avec la Délégation provinciale de la Santé et de la Protection sociale, en collaboration avec la Province d'Al Haouz et avec le soutien de l'association « Sanad ». Cette mission médicale visait à rapprocher les services de santé spécialisés des habitants de la province et à faciliter leur accès aux examens médicaux ainsi qu'aux interventions chirurgicales nécessaires, notamment au profit des populations issues des zones reculées. La phase des interventions chirurgicales a été précédée d'une vaste campagne de dépistage et d'examens médicaux menée dans les centres de santé relevant des différentes communes territoriales de la province, dont ont bénéficié environ 2.372 personnes. À l'issue de ces examens, 700 cas de cataracte nécessitant une intervention chirurgicale ont été diagnostiqués et sélectionnés. Les opérations ont été réalisées par une équipe médicale spécialisée relevant de l'association Sanad, en coordination avec les professionnels de santé de l'hôpital de proximité d'Aït Ourir et avec la participation de plusieurs bénévoles. Une campagne médicale similaire devrait être organisée dans les prochains mois à l'hôpital provincial de Tahannaout, afin d'élargir le nombre de bénéficiaires et de couvrir l'ensemble des communes territoriales de la province. items.title: Financial pressures, vote buying shut women out of politics – Rosemond Atutonu
items.description: The Executive Director of Global Action for Women Empowerment, Rosemond Ewoenam Atutonu, says financial pressures and vote-buying practices continue to prevent many capable women from participating fully in Ghana’s political leadership. According to her, although women play critical roles in supporting their families and communities, the responsibilities placed on them often limit their ability to pursue political ambitions. Speaking at the JoyNews’ Impact Makers Foundation dialogue on “Democracy Is Not For Sale” on Friday, July 31, Ms Atutonu explained that many women are forced to prioritise household needs over political aspirations. “Women are the supports of their families. They are always thinking about what my children will eat, what the entire household will eat,” she said. She noted that these responsibilities leave many women with little time and resources to engage in political activities or seek leadership positions from the local assembly level to national office. Ms Atutonu said some women who show interest in leadership are also discouraged by the financial demands associated with elections, including allegations of having to pay money to secure votes. She recalled experiences from efforts by her organisation to support women contesting assembly and unit committee positions, where some communities demanded financial incentives before offering their support. “It’s like you need to grease our palms for us to even select you as assembly member or even vote you in as a unit committee member,” she stated. She explained that while some women supported by civil society organisations were able to mobilise their communities, others eventually withdrew due to the intense competition and financial pressures. Ms Atutonu stressed that the situation prevents individuals with good ideas and the capacity to serve from progressing into leadership positions simply because they lack the resources to compete. “Probably that person has the ideas, but then because of money, the person cannot go forward,” she added. She called for reforms to make political participation more accessible and reduce the influence of money in Ghana’s democratic processes.

items.title: Photos: Ghana bids farewell to Ambassador James Victor Gbeho
items.description: The Government of Ghana on Friday, July 31, held a state funeral for former Minister for Foreign Affairs and former President of the ECOWAS Commission, Ambassador James Victor Gbeho, in honour of his distinguished service to Ghana, the West African sub-region and the international community. The ceremony, held at the forecourt of the State House in Accra, drew President John Dramani Mahama, Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang, Speaker of Parliament Alban Sumana Kingsford Bagbin, former President of Namibia Dr Nangolo Mbumba, Members of Parliament, government officials, National Democratic Congress (NDC) executives, members of the diplomatic corps, representatives of the United Nations, traditional leaders, family members, friends, sympathisers and other dignitaries from within and outside Ghana. The solemn service featured prayers, the singing of hymns, choral renditions, scripture readings, tributes and the laying of wreaths in honour of the late statesman. The Vice President led the wreath-laying ceremony, followed by members of the bereaved family and representatives of institutions with which Ambassador Gbeho served during his long and distinguished career. Although the ceremony was marked by reflection and solemnity, the atmosphere was one of gratitude and celebration of a life devoted to public service. Many mourners paid tribute to Ambassador Gbeho’s enduring legacy, noting that his remarkable contributions to diplomacy and nation-building would continue to inspire future generations. Ambassador Gbeho died on June 13, 2026, at the age of 91. He rose through the ranks of Ghana’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs to become Chief Director, Deputy Minister and later Minister for Foreign Affairs. He also served as the United Nations Secretary-General’s Special Representative for Somalia and later as President of the ECOWAS Commission, where he championed regional integration and cooperation. Widely regarded as one of Ghana’s finest diplomats, Ambassador Gbeho dedicated more than five decades to public service, earning respect both at home and abroad for his professionalism, humility and commitment to peace and diplomacy.

items.title: African Union condemns drone attack on Egypt’s Port of Damietta
items.description: The African Union (AU) Commission has condemned the recent drone attack targeting vessels stationed at Egypt’s Port of Damietta, describing the incident as a serious violation of the sovereignty and territorial integrity of an African Union member state. In a statement issued on July 31, the Chairperson of the AU Commission, Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, denounced the attack, which occurred on July 29, and reaffirmed the continental body’s solidarity with the Government and people of Egypt. The AU Commission described the drone strike on vessels at the Port of Damietta as an unacceptable attack on a key civilian maritime facility. Chairperson Mahmoud Ali Youssouf said the incident represented more than an isolated security breach, stressing that it challenged the sovereignty of an African nation and underscored the need for greater vigilance in protecting strategic infrastructure across the continent. “The attack constitutes a serious violation of the sovereignty and territorial integrity of an African Union Member State,” the statement said. The African Union expressed its full support for Egypt following the incident, reaffirming its commitment to stand alongside the country as investigations continue. The Commission also commended the Egyptian authorities for what it described as their swift and effective response to the attack, noting that their actions prevented any loss of life despite the seriousness of the incident. The AU further expressed confidence in the ongoing investigations aimed at determining the circumstances surrounding the attack and identifying those responsible. Beyond condemning the attack, the AU Chairperson warned that Africa must not become an arena for conflicts originating outside the continent. Mahmoud Ali Youssouf stressed that the continent’s ports, transport networks and other critical civilian infrastructure should not be exposed to the consequences of external geopolitical disputes. He said safeguarding African territory from the spillover of international conflicts remains essential to preserving peace, stability and economic development across the continent. The African Union called on all parties to exercise maximum restraint and pursue measures aimed at reducing tensions. The Commission reiterated its commitment to the principles of international law and urged all actors to respect the rules governing the protection of civilian infrastructure and maritime navigation. According to the AU, ensuring the safety and security of international shipping routes remains critical for global commerce and regional stability. The organisation also reaffirmed its long-standing commitment to protecting civilian infrastructure from attacks during periods of conflict, warning that such facilities are essential to the livelihoods and economic wellbeing of millions of Africans.

items.title: End killings, casual butchery – Wole Soyinka tasks Tinubu
items.description: By Davies Iheamnachor Nobel Laureate Professor Wole Soyinka has called on President Bola Tinubu to end all forms of killings by state actors, adding that the silence of residents also worsen the situation. This was as Soyinka dedicated his 2026 public lecture to the victims of Nigeria’s extrajudicial killings and state excesses, declaring that the nation’s greatest failure is not only the murders but the collective silence that allows killers to walk free. Soyinka, who made the remarks at the 28th Wole Soyinka Lectures which held in Port Harcourt with the theme “Reclaiming the Nigerian State through Accountability, Justice and Civic Courage” noted that the inactions of the masses towards State excesses fuels more human right abuses and infringements. Through his remarks, he said, he was paying honour to those who had lost their lives because of the state’s deficiencies which has led to the devaluation of human life. He said: “Today is dedicated to the 18 Ughelli residents butchered by state agencies for no reason at all, simply for minding their own business; to the young man shot dead in broad daylight by a policeman while under suspicion; and to Deborah, the youth hunted through the city by her own classmates, necklaced and set ablaze. “The crime is the silence of the rest of us, that such a thing is possible and that the killers of that girl can actually go on television, hold up a match and say, ‘This is the match with which I set her on fire.’ And there the system of justice fails us completely.” Soyinka dismissed critics who accused him of stoking religious conflict whenever he highlights such cases of abuses, noting that sessions like that in Port Harcourt are vital, precisely, to remind Nigerians that the human unit is the least common denominator and the most important element of the community. He called on citizens to keep watch with him over the case of the policeman who shot the young man in the South, and to demand that the justice system not fail again. In his keynote address, Former Minister of Aviation, Chief Osita Chidoka, argued that justice for most Nigerians starts long even before any courtroom. Chidoka said justice starts when police officers decide when a complaint is believed or ignored based on merit and not on external factors. While citing the wrongs in the Nigerian justice and correctional System, Chidoka revealed that 64 per cent of inmates in custodial centres including more than 50,000 Nigerians are awaiting trial and have not been convicted of any crime. He said: “Each of these 50,000 is a life in suspension, a job lost, a family destabilised, someone’s health failings. When the state causes that delay, and the citizens pay for it in lost liberty. The delay is not inefficiency, It is a form of violence carried out by the state itself.” The former minister insisted that true justice means the rules do not change with a citizen’s identity; and prosecution of individuals must follow evidence while those in detention must remain visible to their lawyers. He said: “A citizen who defeats government in court must not face a second battle to compel obedience. Justice is also tested by how society treats those it dislikes. The law is not established when it protects only our friends, Justice must defends the accused, the unpopular, the political opponent, and the minority, because citizenship does not depend on agreement. Where justice is negotiable, citizenship becomes hierarchical.” he added. Earlier in his opening remarks, the chairman of the occasion and former managing director of Niger Delta Development Commission, Chief Timi Alaibe, while drawing from his years in public service said sustainable development cannot exist where accountability is absent. Alaibe urged participants from government, the private sector, academia and civil society to resist treating the 28th Wole Soyinka Lectures as another ceremonial event. Instead, he called for honest reflection and renewed commitment to rebuilding the nation. He said: “Nations are not reclaimed by rhetoric alone, they are reclaimed when conscience triumphs over confidence. When institutions are stronger than individuals. When citizens summon the courage to do what is right, even when it is difficult.” Vanguard News The post End killings, casual butchery – Wole Soyinka tasks Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Godfred Dame rejects blame over Sedina Attionu acquittal, accuses gov’t of political diversion
items.description: Former Attorney-General and Minister for Justice Godfred Yeboah Dame has strongly rejected attempts to hold him or the previous Akufo-Addo administration responsible for the acquittal of former Chief Executive Officer of the Microfinance and Small Loans Centre (MASLOC), Sedina Tamakloe Attionu, describing claims by government communicators as “false and devious”. In a statement issued on Friday, Mr Dame accused communicators of the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC), as well as what he described as “agents and hirelings of the Government”, of deliberately seeking to shift responsibility for the Court of Appeal’s decision onto the former administration. He maintained that the official record clearly demonstrates that neither he nor the Office of the Attorney-General under his tenure failed in handling the appeal process. Mr Dame stated that throughout his tenure as Attorney-General, the Office of the Attorney-General was never served with any notice of appeal allegedly filed by Madam Attionu in 2024. According to him, state attorneys informed the Court of Appeal in both oral and written submissions in April 2026 that they had only become aware of the appeal after the court directed both parties to file written submissions. “No notice of an appeal filed by Sedina Attionu in 2024 came to the attention of the Office of Attorney-General in my tenure,” he said. He further argued that even if such an appeal had indeed been filed in 2024, it remained inconsequential because no further action was taken by the appellant until after the National Democratic Congress returned to office. “As such, the Republic had no action to take in 2024 regarding the appeal,” he maintained. The former Attorney-General also defended his handling of the criminal case after securing Madam Attionu’s conviction, insisting that his office pursued every legal avenue to ensure she returned to Ghana to serve her sentence. He disclosed that extradition proceedings initiated by his office culminated in a ruling by the United States District Court for the District of Nevada on April 9, which upheld the extradition request and ordered that Madam Attionu remain in custody pending the approval of the United States Secretary of State. Mr Dame noted that throughout the extradition proceedings, which spanned from July 2024 to April 2026, there was no indication that an appeal had been filed in Ghana. “At no stage during the extradition proceedings was any appeal filed in 2024 mentioned, including in documents submitted by Sedina Attionu herself before the U.S. District Court,” he stated. Mr Dame explained that lawyers for Madam Attionu obtained leave from the Court of Appeal on February 10, 2026 to file their written submissions and subsequently filed them on February 12, 2026. He emphasised that by that time, he was no longer serving as Attorney-General. According to his account, prosecuting state attorneys were surprised when they received the appellant’s written submissions on February 16, 2026, having never previously been notified of the appeal. The prosecution later filed its own submissions opposing the appeal and sought leave from the court to submit them out of time on April 9. Mr Dame said the prosecution’s submissions highlighted several procedural concerns, including what it described as an incomplete record of appeal, omitted prosecution exhibits and the late notification of the appeal proceedings. The former Attorney-General further explained that the Court of Appeal, presided over by Justice Mensah Datsa, directed that three volumes of the Record of Appeal be provided to the Republic because they had not previously been made available. Following a review of those records, the Republic successfully applied on May 28 to include three additional documents in the appeal record before the matter was adjourned to June 17. Mr Dame stressed that these proceedings all occurred after he had left office. On June 17, a differently constituted panel of the Court of Appeal, presided over by Justice Ankamah, heard the appeal and reserved judgment, which eventually resulted in Madam Attionu’s acquittal. Beyond defending his own record, Mr Dame criticised the current government’s handling of criminal prosecutions, arguing that the acquittal has generated understandable public concern given the evidence presented during the original trial. He suggested that the outcome reflected what he described as a broader trend by the current Attorney-General to discontinue criminal cases involving leading members and affiliates of the National Democratic Congress. Mr Dame compared the handling of the Sedina Attionu case to the long-running Alfred Agbesi Woyome saga, arguing that the justice system must apply the law equally regardless of political affiliation. He further questioned what he described as an apparent contradiction between the government’s decision to discontinue cases involving some of its own members while simultaneously pursuing the Operation Recover All Loot (ORAL) initiative and prosecuting individuals associated with the opposition. The former Attorney-General urged Ghanaians to demand greater accountability in the administration of justice, insisting that prosecutorial decisions must be guided by the law rather than political considerations. He argued that public confidence in the justice system would be undermined if political allies were perceived to receive favourable treatment while opponents faced more aggressive prosecution. “A justice system where political allies avoid accountability while political opponents face unequal treatment undermines confidence in the rule of law and reflects poorly on the State,” he said.

items.title: Boulgou : le CSPS de Zonsé enregistre une baisse de 79% des cas de paludisme au premier semestre 2026
items.description: Boulgou : le CSPS de Zonsé enregistre une baisse de 79% des cas de paludisme au premier semestre 2026 Zonsé, le 29 juillet 2026 (AIB)-Le Centre de santé et de promotion sociale (CSPS) de Zonsé a enregistré une baisse d'environ 79% des cas de paludisme au premier semestre 2026, par rapport à la même période en 2025. Le bilan a été présenté mercredi, lors de l'assemblée générale de redevabilité convoquée par le major du CSPS, le camarade P. Eugène Wangré. La rencontre s'est tenue en présence des responsables des services déconcentrés, des chefs coutumiers, des leaders religieux et des représentants des communautés de la commune. Selon le major Wangré, cette assemblée vise à rendre compte des activités du centre et à renforcer l'implication communautaire pour l'amélioration de l'offre de soins. Du bilan présenté, il ressort que le CSPS a réalisé 3 076 consultations au premier semestre 2026, contre 2 086 à la même période en 2025, soit une hausse de plus de 47%. Sur la même période, les cas de paludisme sont passés de 897 à 189, une performance que les responsables attribuent aux campagnes de sensibilisation, à l'utilisation des moustiquaires imprégnées d'insecticide et aux actions d'assainissement. En santé maternelle, 376 accouchements assistés ont été enregistrés, contre 347 en 2025. Les inscriptions en consultation prénatale de rang 1 (CPN1) sont également en hausse, passant de 363 à 438. Toutefois, les agents de santé ont insisté sur la nécessité, pour les femmes enceintes, de consulter dès le premier trimestre de la grossesse afin de prévenir les complications. Ils ont aussi appelé à renforcer la sensibilisation sur la planification familiale et le respect du calendrier des consultations prénatales. Deux causeries éducatives ont porté sur la prévention de la tuberculose et l'importance des consultations précoces pendant la grossesse. Le bilan financier du semestre, ainsi que les dons reçus des ressortissants et de la diaspora de Zonsé, ont également été présentés, dans un souci de transparence. Les participants ont salué la qualité des prestations offertes par le CSPS et rendu un hommage particulier au maïeuticien, le camarade Sana Karim, pour son professionnalisme, son sens de l'écoute et le respect témoigné aux femmes enceintes et aux parturientes. Enfin, les responsables du CSPS ont exprimé leur gratitude au Président de la Délégation spéciale de la commune de Zonsé, le camarade Wendinmi Frédéric Ouédraogo, pour son accompagnement constant, notamment pour le maintien en service de l'ambulance communale. Agence d'Information du Burkina AG/SM/ata

items.title: Emerse Fae leaves role as Ivory Coast coach
items.description: Emerse Fae has left his role as Ivory Coast coach after his contract expired and was not renewed, the Ivorian Football Federation (FIF) said on Friday. “The contract of Mr Emerse Fae, head coach of the Ivory Coast national team, expired on July 31, 2026 and will not be renewed,” the federation said in a statement. Fae led Ivory Coast to an Africa Cup of Nations title on home soil two years ago, taking charge midway through the tournament after Frenchman Jean-Louis Gasset was sacked during the group stage. Initially named on an interim basis, Fae was later confirmed in the role after leading Ivory Coast to a third continental crown with a 2-1 victory over Nigeria in the final. He subsequently guided the Elephants to qualification for the 2026 World Cup. They reached the knockout phase for the first time before losing to Norway in the last 32. The FIF praised Fae’s contribution to the national team, saying the progress and results under his leadership would remain “an important part of the recent history of Ivorian football.” The federation said it would announce Fae’s successor as coach at a later date. The post Emerse Fae leaves role as Ivory Coast coach appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Basketball : NBA Africa et de la Basketball Africa League (BAL) explorent des pistes innovantes pour le financement et la professionnalisation
items.description: Lomé, 31 juil. (ATOP) – Une table ronde sur les mécanismes innovants de financement et à la professionnalisation du basketball au Togo a réuni, le vendredi 31 juillet à Lomé, une délégation de NBA Africa et de la Basketball Africa League (BAL), conduite par la directrice de NBA Africa, Akamanzi Clare, et le ministre en charge du Sport, Dr. Abdul-Fahd Fofana La séance a été présidée par le ministre délégué Fofana, qui avait à ses côtés les acteurs publics, les responsables des instances sportives, du secteur privé et les partenaires au développement. Elle a enregistré aussi la présence d’Arthur Lilas Trimua, ministre délégué auprès du ministre de l’Economie et de la Veille stratégique, chargé de la promotion des investissements et de la souveraineté économique. Placée sous le thème « Quels mécanismes innovants pour le financement et la professionnalisation du basketball au Togo ? », la table-ronde servi de cadre pour explorer les perspectives d’un partenariat stratégique pour structurer et dynamiser l’écosystème du Basketball au Togo. Vue Partielle des présidents de fédérations sportives Les discussions ont porté sur les principaux leviers ayant permis à certains pays africains de développer leur écosystème de basketball, ainsi que sur les mécanismes innovants de financement susceptibles de soutenir les infrastructures sportives, les centres de formation et les clubs. Les participants ont également analysé les moyens de renforcer l’implication du secteur privé togolais dans le financement et le développement du basketball national, notamment à travers le sponsoring, le mécénat sportif, les partenariats avec les clubs et l’accompagnement des jeunes talents. Les échanges ont aussi permis d’examiner les stratégies permettant aux acteurs privés souhaitant investir dans le basketball d’optimiser leurs partenariats, de créer davantage de valeur et de maximiser leur retour sur investissement. La réflexion a enfin porté sur le développement des métiers liés à la pratique du basketball, afin de faire de cette discipline une véritable filière d’insertion professionnelle pour les jeunes. Il ressort que le Togo dispose d’importantes opportunités pour faire du basketball un outil d’éducation, d’inclusion sociale et de création d’emplois pour les jeunes. Toutefois, la valorisation de ce potentiel nécessite une démarche structurée impliquant l’ensemble des acteurs, notamment l’Etat, les fédérations sportives, les partenaires techniques et financiers ainsi que les entreprises privées. Dr Abdul-Fahd Fofana a assuré que les recommandations issues de la table ronde seront analysées et prises en compte dans les prochaines actions du gouvernement. Il a réaffirmé la volonté des autorités de collaborer avec le secteur privé pour construire un véritable écosystème sportif, notamment autour du basketball, capable de former les jeunes, de créer des emplois, de stimuler la croissance économique et de renforcer la cohésion sociale. Parmi les priorités identifiées, précise le ministre, figurent le développement d’infrastructures sportives de proximité dans les établissements scolaires, l’étude d’un projet d’aréna aux normes internationales, la promotion du basketball comme outil d’insertion des jeunes et le renforcement des opportunités d’emploi liées à l’industrie sportive. Il a appelé à un partenariat durable entre les pouvoirs publics et les acteurs économiques pour assurer le développement du basketball togolais. La directrice de NBA Afrique a fait savoir que le basketball constitue un levier de développement économique, d’éducation, d’entrepreneuriat, de création d’emplois et d’impact social pour la jeunesse africaine. Elle a souligné que l’Afrique, avec sa population très jeune et son important réservoir de talents, dispose d’un fort potentiel dans cette discipline, qui nécessite toutefois des structures adaptées pour être pleinement valorisé. « Près de 10 % des joueurs de la NBA ont des origines africaines, preuve du potentiel du continent. Le véritable défi n’est donc pas le talent, mais la mise en place de systèmes performants, d’infrastructures de qualité, de partenariats solides et de parcours de formation capables de transformer ce potentiel en valeur économique durable », a-t-elle indiqué. Le vice-président du Conseil national du patronat du Togo (CNP-Togo), Badohu Yiva, a indiqué que le développement du sport, notamment du basketball, doit désormais reposer sur un modèle économique structuré plutôt que sur des subventions ponctuelles. Il a plaidé pour des partenariats gagnant-gagnant entre les entreprises et les acteurs sportifs, fondés sur la transparence, la bonne gouvernance, le professionnalisme et des résultats mesurables. NBA Africa et Basketball Africa League (BAL) sont deux institutions panafricaines œuvrant pour le développement du basketball sur le continent, à travers la détection de talents, la réhabilitation d’infrastructures et la formation des acteurs. ATOP/AR/AO/KYA

items.title: Gold Fields Ghana Foundation expands healthcare access as over 260 residents renew NHIS in Awudua outreach
items.description: More than 260 residents of Awudua and surrounding communities in the Western Region have gained renewed access to healthcare after registering, renewing or replacing their National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS) cards during a free medical outreach organised by the Gold Fields Ghana Foundation. The outreach, held in partnership with Unilever Ghana and Diagnostic Centre Limited, also provided free screening for Hepatitis B, HIV, tuberculosis and other health conditions as part of activities marking World Hepatitis Day. Foundation officials said the Health Engagement Access Link (HEAL) Programme, which cost more than GH¢452,000 to implement, was designed to bring essential healthcare services closer to residents who often face challenges accessing specialised medical care. In addition to the 265 people who benefited from NHIS registration, renewal or card replacement, the programme recorded 180 Hepatitis B screenings, 121 HIV screenings, 98 eye care consultations, 70 Ear, Nose and Throat (ENT) consultations, 50 dental screenings and 46 tuberculosis screenings. Residents also received blood glucose, blood pressure, malaria, typhoid and haemoglobin tests, as well as ultrasound scans, X-ray services, spirometry and free medication. A major feature of the outreach was the provision of free laboratory and diagnostic investigations through a partnership with Diagnostic Centre Limited. The company sponsored all diagnostic tests, including Hepatitis B, HIV, haemoglobin, blood glucose, typhoid screening, ultrasound scans, X-rays and spirometry, enabling residents to access specialised services at no cost. Unilever Ghana also donated personal and household hygiene products, including toothpaste, bathing soap and laundry soap, to beneficiaries to reinforce health education on oral and personal hygiene beyond the one-day exercise. Executive Secretary of the Gold Fields Ghana Foundation, Abdel-Razak Yakubu, said the Foundation’s objective is to reduce barriers to healthcare by taking medical services directly to communities. “We bring the hospital to the doorstep of the community folks. That’s our focus: preventive healthcare,” he said. The HEAL Programme forms part of the Foundation’s broader community investment strategy, which focuses on improving access to quality healthcare while promoting disease prevention and early diagnosis in its host communities.

items.title: Défense des droits de l’Homme : vers la création du « Prix national des droits de l’Homme »
items.description: Pour mieux renforcer la défense des droits de l’homme au Sénégal, la présidente de la Commission nationale des droits de l’homme (CNDH), le Pr. Amsatou Sow Sidibé, a fait part vendredi, au chef de l’Etat, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, de son ambition de créer le « Prix national des Droits de l’Homme ». Le Prix national des Droits de l’homme participe, selon le chef de l’État, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, à l’ancrage des valeurs citoyennes et républicaines qui fondent le vivre-ensemble au Sénégal. « Je voudrais ainsi saluer votre initiative de créer le « Prix national des Droits de l'Homme ». Je vous remercie du prix d'honneur que la Commission m'a décerné en décembre 2025. J'y vois moins une distinction personnelle qu'un encouragement adressé à la Nation tout entière », a-t-il dit vendredi, lors de la réception des rapports d’activité 2023, 2024 et 2025 de la Commission nationale des droits de l’homme (CNDH). A lire aussi : CNDH : les rapports annuels d’activités 2023, 2024 et 2025 transmis au chef de l’Etat Au-delà de sa dimension symbolique, ce prix participe, d’après le président Faye, à l'ancrage des valeurs citoyennes et républicaines qui fondent le vivre-ensemble sénégalais. Il sensibilise et mobilise autour des enjeux liés aux droits humains. Il estime que ce prix encourage aussi les bonnes pratiques des acteurs engagés pour la dignité humaine, la justice et l'égalité. Il constitue également un instrument de sensibilisation et de mobilisation autour des enjeux liés aux droits humains. « J'ai pris connaissance avec un intérêt particulier de votre proposition d’institutionnaliser cette distinction afin d'en assurer la pérennité. Votre demande est pertinente et j’instruis les départements ministériels compétents à vous accompagner dans cette initiative », a-t-il affirmé. Sur ce, ils étudieront également la proposition de la présidente de la CNDH, de placer l’Edition 2026 du Prix national des Droits de l’Homme consacrée aux droits des personnes handicapées, sous son haut patronage. « Le choix de cette thématique traduit notre ambition commune de construire une société plus juste et plus inclusive. A ce titre, l’adoption des décrets d’application de la loi d’orientation sur les personnes handicapées, que vous avez évoquée, sera étudiée », a-t-il relevé. Relancer le processus d’adoption du code de l’enfant Ainsi, le chef de l’État a annoncé que des dispositions seront également prises pour étudier la relance du processus d’adoption du code de l’enfant, dans une démarche plus inclusive et participative tenant compte de nos valeurs culturelles. Sur les conditions de détention, souligne-t-il, un vaste programme est en cours. Il vise à améliorer substantiellement la prise en charge des détenus et à humaniser davantage l'univers carcéral. En outre, conformément à la politique pénale du Sénégal, le ministre de la Justice, Garde des Sceaux, veillera à ce que la liberté reste le principe et la détention l’exception. Concernant l’amélioration de la situation des droits humains à travers le pays, le président de la République a soutenu que la réaccréditation au statut « A » constitue une priorité nationale. Dès lors, il a instruit le ministre de la Justice, Garde des Sceaux, de conduire dans les meilleurs délais le processus de désignation des commissaires, selon une procédure ouverte, transparente et inclusive. « D'autres mesures d'accompagnement suivront, notamment sur les moyens de fonctionnement et les conditions d'installation de l'institution. Vos besoins feront l'objet d'un examen attentif. Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de l'Agenda national de transformation Sénégal 2050, nous poursuivrons les réformes nécessaires. Nous voulons bâtir un État de droit toujours plus fort, plus juste et plus protecteur des droits et libertés de chaque citoyenne et de chaque citoyen », a-t-il indiqué. Mariama DIEME

items.title: Ouahigouya : des produits frauduleux d’une valeur de plus de 100 millions de francs incinérés
items.description: Ouahigouya : des produits frauduleux d'une valeur de plus de 100 millions de francs incinérés Ouahigouya, 31 juil. 2026 (AIB)-Les autorités administratives et judiciaires ont procédé le jeudi 30 juillet à l'incinération de produits frauduleux d’une valeur de plus de 100 millions FCFA, saisis jugés impropres à la consommation, a constaté l'AIB sur place. Dans le cadre de la lutte contre la fraude, la contrebande et le trafic de produits illicites dans la région de Yaadga, les autorités ont procédé à la destruction de produits frauduleusement introduits sur le marché et jugés dangereux sur la santé de la population et sur l'environnement. Ce sont des produits composés de cartons de cigarettes, des produits pharmaceutiques prohibés, des bouteilles d'alcool, de la drogue, des produits de consommation courante, le tout estimé à plus de 50 tonnes et d'une valeur de plus de 100 millions de nos francs qui ont été incinérés à Ouahigouya. Pour l'autorité régionale représentée par le secrétaire général de la région de Yaadga, Kuilga Albert Zongo, deux lots de produits ont été incinérés à savoir des produits périmés et ceux prohibés confisqués et scellés par le Tribunal de grande instance de Ouahigouya. Il a souligné que cette destruction a pour but de protéger la santé de la population et de les préserver des impacts négatifs de la fraude. Le Procureur du Faso, près le tribunal de grande instance de Ouahigouya, Aly Benjamin Coulibaly a laissé entendre que cette activité répond à une prescription légale du code de procédure pénal en son article 242-14 et plus précisément à l'alinéa 6 qui prescrit que le procureur du Faso a la possibilité de procéder à la destruction des produits lorsqu'il estime que la conservation de ces produits est dangereuse pour la communauté ou lorsque les auteurs de ces biens ne viennent pas les réclamer durant un certain temps. Pour le Directeur régional de l'industrie, du commerce et de l'artisanat de Yaadga, Mahamadi Zoré, « l'incinération est un mot à l'endroit d'une certaine catégorie de commerçants pour leur dire que le département du commerce est organisé et engagé à combattre la fraude dans tous les lieux possibles ». « J'invite les acteurs économiques à respecter la réglementation et à se conformer à la loi au lieu de chercher des bénéfices inutiles sur certains secteurs où ils peuvent regretter inutilement car les indélicats pris sont contraints de quitter le marché », a-t-il. Agence d'Information du Burkina AZ/PN/AS/ATA

items.title: L’AJS appelle à transformer les droits des femmes en leviers d’action
items.description: À l’occasion de la Journée internationale de la Femme africaine (JIFA), célébrée ce 31 juillet, l’Association des Juristes Sénégalaises (AJS) plaide pour une consolidation des acquis en matière de droits des femmes et appelle à une mobilisation accrue de tous les acteurs afin de faire de l’égalité un moteur du développement du continent. Dans un communiqué publié ce jour, l’AJS rend hommage à « la contribution essentielle des femmes africaines au développement économique, social, culturel et politique du continent ». L’organisation estime que cette journée constitue à la fois un moment de bilan sur les avancées enregistrées en matière de reconnaissance et de protection des droits des femmes, mais aussi une occasion de réfléchir aux conditions de leur pleine participation à l’Afrique de demain. L’association rappelle que le Sénégal a franchi plusieurs étapes importantes grâce à la ratification du Protocole de Maputo, à l’adoption de réformes législatives et à la mise en œuvre de politiques publiques visant à renforcer l’égalité entre les femmes et les hommes. Elle souligne toutefois que le principal défi réside désormais dans la consolidation de ces acquis. Pour l’AJS, cette ambition passe notamment par un meilleur accès des femmes à la justice, à l’éducation, à l’emploi, au foncier, au financement et aux opportunités économiques, ainsi que par leur présence effective dans les espaces de décision. L’organisation insiste également sur la nécessité de renforcer l’autonomisation économique et le leadership féminin, tout en accordant une attention particulière aux filles et aux jeunes femmes, considérées comme un potentiel majeur pour l’avenir du continent. Dans cette dynamique, l’Association des Juristes Sénégalaises invite les pouvoirs publics, les collectivités territoriales, le secteur privé, la société civile et les partenaires au développement à intensifier leurs efforts pour faire des droits des femmes de véritables opportunités de participation à la vie économique, sociale et politique. « Les droits des femmes sont des droits humains. Leur effectivité est une exigence de justice et un facteur essentiel du développement de notre continent », affirme l’AJS, qui appelle à poursuivre cette dynamique « avec confiance et détermination » afin que les femmes soient pleinement reconnues comme des actrices et partenaires du développement de l’Afrique de demain. A.N

items.title: Civic education on vote buying must translate into action, not just awareness – NCCE
items.description: The Programme Director of the National Commission for Civic Education (NCCE) in charge of General Services, Imurana Mohammed, has called for a shift from vote-buying awareness campaigns to practical action, arguing that civic education can only be effective if it influences citizens’ behaviour. Speaking at the JoyNews’ Impact Makers Foundation “Democracy Is Not for Sale” public forum, Mr Mohammed said while the NCCE continues to educate political party activists, particularly the youth, on laws governing public order, lasting democratic change requires more than classroom-style sensitisation. He explained that the Commission has established inter-party dialogue committees with district-level structures across the country to provide platforms where political parties can resolve disagreements before they escalate into conflict. Mr Mohammed, however, stressed that civic education should not be measured by the number of awareness campaigns conducted but by the extent to which they change attitudes and behaviour. “One of the constraints to civic education is the fact that we do education, but nobody sits an exam for our education. If you go and do the education and leave it at that, then you are not doing civic education,” he said in Ho on Friday, July 31. To bridge that gap, he said the NCCE collaborates with civil society organisations to ensure that public education translates into meaningful democratic participation. As part of those efforts, the Commission has partnered with the Centre for Democratic Development (CDD-Ghana) to organise public forums across all 10 regional capitals to gather citizens’ views on the proposed Political Party Financing Bill. Mr Mohammed said sustained collaboration, grassroots dialogue and practical civic engagement remain essential to promoting accountability, peaceful political participation and strengthening Ghana’s democracy.

items.title: Italy suspends Schengen agreement with Spain: foreign minister
items.description: Italy has suspended its Schengen agreement with Spain, Italy’s Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said on Friday, calling the measure “unavoidable”. “The temporary suspension of Schengen with Spain is a necessary choice to safeguard the security of our citizens and defend the European borders,” he wrote in a post on X. He noted that the influx of migrants in Ceuta, Spain, “reminds us that the management of the Union’s borders is a shared responsibility among our countries, one toward the other”. “We must work together to prevent uncontrolled migrant flows from entering EU territory, with all the consequent risks and the threat of terrorism, which must be countered without hesitation,” he added. US President Donald Trump led far-right attempts on Friday on both sides of the Atlantic to make political capital from Spain’s migration crisis, portraying the migrant surge in Ceuta as a warning for America if his opponents get into power. “It’s terrible. Remember that picture. That’s going to be us in three years if the wrong side gets in,” Trump was quoted as saying by Fox News . “If the Democrats get in, you will not live a very good life.” With polls showing Trump’s support has fallen into the low 30 per cent range and opposition Democrats hoping to win at least partial control of Congress in November midterm elections, the crisis in Spain offers Republicans a chance to return to one of their political strongpoints. News footage of migrants overwhelming barriers to get into Ceuta — a tiny Spanish territory on the Moroccan coast — aired repeatedly on Fox News and went viral across right-wing Trump-allied social media accounts. In Europe, far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) co-leader Alice Weidel claimed in an X post that “Ceuta was left in ruins overnight” by the mass influx from Morocco. She argued that Germany is “likely the destination for most of these migrants”. “Germany must prepare itself: borders must be secured and rejections rigorously enforced,” wrote Weidel, whose party is backed by top Trump officials. Both Italy’s right-wing prime minister Giorgia Meloni and the populist right-wing ruling coalition in Finland called for excluding Spain from the European visa-free zone as a result of the situation. Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babis, a billionaire Trump supporter, said the Ceuta situation was caused by Spain’s policy of offering hundreds of thousands of migrants already in the country a legal status. “They are replacing Spaniards with migrants,” Babis said. ‘Invasion of the West’ Trump’s election victory over Democrat Kamala Harris in 2024 was fueled by voter worries over uncontrolled migration on the US-Mexico border and his lurid warnings of migrants coming to murder Americans and even to eat their pets. Trump’s vice president, JD Vance, posted news footage on Friday of migrants pouring into Ceuta on X and wrote it highlighted “radical left-wing globalist policies that have enabled the Invasion of the West.” “These images out of Spain are an unfortunate reminder of the consequences of mass migration,” Vance posted on X. Late on Thursday, White House Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, a chief architect of Trump’s anti-migration crackdown, posted video of the Ceuta crisis and said, “Democrats will see your home trampled and stolen by invaders and they will rejoice.”

items.title: ACP Wilson warns politicians against election gifts, calls practice a ‘crime scene’
items.description: A senior police officer has warned politicians against distributing food and other items during elections, describing such acts as potential vote buying and urging citizens to reject practices that undermine the integrity of Ghana’s democratic process. ACP Brown Mercy Wilson, Head of Legal and Prosecution for the Volta Region, made the comments at the JoyNews’ “Democracy Is Not For Sale” forum organised by the JoyNews Impact Makers Foundation. According to her, politicians who engage in such activities during elections create an environment that could compromise free and fair decision-making by voters. “When a politician is holding packs of food and sharing during an election, that politician is not a nice person. That environment is a crime scene,” ACP Wilson stated. She urged politicians and public figures to be conscious of their conduct, particularly actions that could influence voters through material inducements. “We are not supposed to do things that will, for want of a better explanation, offend the sense of decency of people who look to you when you are doing your things or when you are saying your things. Don’t do things that will offend their own sense of decency,” she said. Her comments come amid growing national discussions about the influence of money and inducements in Ghana’s electoral processes. The “Democracy Is Not For Sale” forum series, organised by the JoyNews Impact Makers Foundation, has brought together political actors, civil society organisations, legal experts and citizens to discuss concerns surrounding vote buying and the monetisation of politics. A pre-forum survey conducted by JoyNews ahead of the Volta Regional edition showed that many respondents were aware of vote buying, with some indicating that they had witnessed politicians or their agents offering money and other incentives to influence electoral choices. Under Ghana’s electoral laws, vote buying and voter inducement are criminal offences. Sections 240 and 241 of the Criminal Code, 1960 (Act 29), together with provisions under the Representation of the People Act, 1992 (PNDCL 284), prohibit the buying and selling of votes in public elections. However, concerns have been raised about gaps in the law regarding internal political party elections, as party primaries are not classified as public elections under existing legislation. This has led to calls from governance experts and civil society groups for reforms to extend legal sanctions against inducements beyond general elections. The Office of the Special Prosecutor has also expressed interest in investigating allegations of vote buying linked to political party primaries.

items.title: Pakistan welcomes Board of Peace developments under Gaza Peace Plan: PM Shehbaz
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday said that Pakistan welcomed developments under the Board of Peace towards implementing the disarmament process under the Gaza Peace Plan. Earlier today, US President Donald Trump said talks in Cairo between mediators and Hamas leaders on Thursday have led to a phased disarmament agreement in Gaza, but a Hamas official described the deal as a draft and US officials said Israel was sceptical the Palestinian group would surrender its weapons. “Today, the Board of Peace reached a HISTORIC agreement for the COMPLETE DISARMAMENT of Hamas and all other armed groups in Gaza,” Trump said in a social media post, adding that the disarmament would come in phases. In a social media post on X, PM Shehbaz said, “Pakistan welcomes developments under the Board of Peace towards the implementation of the disarmament process under the Gaza Peace Plan.” He emphasised that the mediating countries, including the United States of America, Egypt, Qatar and Turkiye, deserved “special appreciation for their efforts in achieving this progress”. Commending President Trump’s “courageous leadership”, the premier said that this represented “a significant achievement for the Board of Peace”. “Pakistan expresses the hope that with these developments, concrete steps will be taken towards implementing all commitments under the Gaza Peace Plan. He concluded by expressing hope that these efforts would lead to the realisation of the right to self-determination of the Palestinian people through a credible and time-bound political process, in line with international legitimacy and relevant UN resolutions. The prime minister added that this should result in the establishment of an independent, sovereign and contiguous State of Palestine based on the pre-1967 borders, with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital. The board was initially proposed in September 2025 and formally established in January. Under its charter, the US government serves as its official depository and Trump has designated the Donald J Trump Institute of Peace in Washington as the Board’s headquarters. A UN Security Council resolution adopted in mid-November last year authorised the board, along with cooperating states, to establish an international stabilisation force in Gaza following a ceasefire that began in October under a Trump-backed plan accepted by Israel and Hamas. Pakistan is among the 14 countries that signed the charter of the Board of Peace on January 22 on the sidelines of the World Economic Forum in Davos, becoming a founding member of the body. The list of founding members also includes Argentina, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Albania, Bahrain, Belarus, Bulgaria, Cambodia, El Salvador, Egypt, Hungary, Indonesia, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Kosovo, Kuwait, Mongolia, Morocco, Paraguay, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, the United Arab Emirates, Uzbekistan, and Vietnam, spanning the Middle East, Asia, Europe, Latin America and the Caucasus. The board was originally conceived to oversee the ceasefire and reconstruction of Gaza, but its charter expands its mandate to peace-building in all areas affected by or at risk of conflict.

items.title: 50 ans de kinésithérapie au Togo : Une conférence de presse pour démarrer la célébration du jubilé d’or
items.description: Lomé, 31 juil. (ATOP) – Une conférence de presse tenue le vendredi 31 juillet à Lomé a servi de lancement officiel, des activités du 5ème congrès international du 50 ème anniversaire de la kinésithérapie au Togo. Organisée par l’Association des kinésithérapeutes du Togo (AKITO), cette initiative vise à célébrer cinquante années de contribution de la kinésithérapie à l’amélioration de la santé, de la réadaptation fonctionnelle et de la qualité de vie des populations togolaises. Cette conférence de presse marque le début d’une série d’activités scientifiques, professionnelles et communautaires sous le thème : « Kinésithérapie face aux enjeux de santé publique au Togo ». Une Caravane de sensibilisation sur la kinésithérapie dans deux localités : Kovié et Dapaong, le 29 août prochain ; des journées portes ouvertes s ur la réadaptation et la kinésithérapie, couplées de dons de matériel et dons de sang les 03 et 04 septembre. Il y aura aussi des activités sportives réunissant les personnes en situation de handicap et professionnels de santé le 24 octobre à l’Africlub karting, des journées scientifiques avec des experts nationaux et internationaux, accompagnées d’un don de sang les 26 et 27 novembre 2026 à Lomé. La clôture du cinquantenaire sera marquée par un dîner de gala dans la soirée du 28 novembre toujours à Lomé. A travers cette célébration, l’AKITO entend rendre hommage aux pionniers de la profession, mettre en lumière les avancées réalisées au Togo et ouvrir des perspectives de développement face aux nouveaux défis de santé publique. De surcroît, l’association veut renforcer la visibilité de la profession, promouvoir le rôle essentiel du kinésithérapeute dans le système de santé et sensibiliser davantage la population à l’importance de la prévention, de la rééducation et de la réadaptation fonctionnelle. Le secrétaire général du ministère en charge de la santé, Dr Wotobé Kokou a rendu hommage aux pionniers de la kinésithérapie qui ont posé les bases de ce jubilé d’or. Il a invité les professionnels du domaine à renforcer la formation et promouvoir l’innovation technologique afin d’améliorer la qualité des prestations de soins. Le président du comite d’organisation des activités du jubile d’or, Akpabli Komlavi et le président de l’AKITO, Akossou Prosper ont salué la rigueur et l’énergie déployée pour la réussite mémorable de ce cinquantenaire. La kinésithérapie ou physiothérapie, est une spécialité paramédicale employant différentes techniques actives (exercices spécifiques de musculation, gymnastique) ou passives (étirements, massage, électrostimulation, mobilisation) en vue de conserver ou de rétablir les fonctions motrices et sensorielles d’un patient. ATOP/GMM/KYA

items.title: Liverpool stars Curtis Jones, Szoboszlai clash in heated on-pitch exchange
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Liverpool midfielders Curtis Jones and Dominik Szoboszlai were involved in a heated on-pitch argument following the Reds’ 1-0 pre-season victory over Wrexham in New York. According to BBC Sport, the pair exchanged words shortly after the final whistle as Liverpool players walked around Yankee Stadium to applaud supporters. Defender Kostas Tsimikas later joined the confrontation, with television footage appearing to show him throwing the captain’s armband onto the pitch during the exchange. The reason behind the disagreement remains unclear, although BBC Sport noted that Szoboszlai handed the captain’s armband to Tsimikas rather than Jones when he was substituted during the match. Asked about the incident, Szoboszlai declined to discuss the details but insisted the squad remains united. We want the best for the club and for each other,” the Hungary international told BBC Sport. “Now that a couple of guys have left and maybe we are not the oldest in the team but we’ve been here a long time, we are all in the same boat and we want the best for the club and for each other.” He added that the players are fully behind captain Virgil van Dijk and manager Andoni Iraola as Liverpool continue adapting under their new head coach. “We have a captain in Virgil [van Dijk] and we will follow him everywhere with what he and the gaffer says and I think I can talk from everybody’s side that we want to be successful this season. “It’s a long term [project] because obviously we have a new manager and the team has been changed. Maybe not in a couple of months but in the long term, I think it will work out.” Liverpool sources, however, played down the incident, maintaining that disagreements between teammates are common in elite football and suggesting the exchange only became public because the players were completing a post-match lap of appreciation rather than returning directly to the dressing room. The incident comes amid continued speculation over Jones’ future after Liverpool rejected a reported £21.7 million bid from Inter Milan earlier this summer. The England midfielder has one year remaining on his contract, with Iraola recently describing him as “a great, great player” and expressing his desire for him to remain at Anfield. items.title: Court jails yahoo boys’ middleman four years for money laundering
items.description: By Innocent Anaba Justice Akintayo Aluko of the Federal High Court sitting in Ikoyi, Lagos, has convicted and sentenced Sunmonu Olasunkanmi Thaoban to four years’ imprisonment for money laundering offences. Sunmonu was prosecuted by the Lagos Zonal Directorate 1 of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) on a two-count charge bordering on money laundering. The EFCC alleged that the convict, while acting as a middleman in 2023, disguised the origin of ₦16 million believed to be proceeds of unlawful activities by converting the funds into a black 2018 G-Wagon Jeep. The prosecution said the offence contravened provisions of the Money Laundering (Prevention and Prohibition) Act, 2022. Sunmonu pleaded guilty to both counts. Following his plea, EFCC counsel, H.U. Kofarnaisa, reviewed the facts of the case and urged the court to convict and sentence him accordingly. Justice Aluko found him guilty and sentenced him to four years’ imprisonment, with an option of a ₦1.8 million fine. The court also ordered the forfeiture of the black G-Wagon Jeep and a mobile device belonging to the convict to the Federal Government. Meanwhile, the court also convicted and sentenced four Bureau de Change (BDC) operators to 12 months’ imprisonment each for engaging in illegal foreign exchange transactions. The convicts — Umar Muhammad Lamido, Yusuf Musa Yusuf, Abdulmuhimin Mahmud and Muhammed Musa — were prosecuted by the EFCC on separate one-count charges bordering on illegal foreign exchange operations. They all pleaded guilty to the charges. After reviewing the facts of the cases, Kofarnaisa urged the court to convict and sentence the defendants accordingly. Justice Aluko subsequently convicted the four BDC operators and sentenced each of them to 12 months’ imprisonment, with an option of a ₦100,000 fine. The EFCC said the convictions reaffirm its commitment to enforcing financial regulations and prosecuting individuals involved in economic crimes. items.title: Journée de la Femme africaine : l’accès à l’eau et l’autonomisation économique au cœur des revendications
items.description: Reunies a Koulikoro ce vendredi 31 juillet a l'occasion de la journee internationale de la femme africaine, les participantes ont appele a accelerer les investissements dans l'acces a l'eau potable et a renforcer l'autonomisation economique des femmes. Les autorites ont, de leur cote, reaffirme leur engagement a ameliorer les infrastructures hydrauliques a travers le pays. Placee sous le theme « l'acces a l'eau pour chaque femme » , cette celebration a rassemble autorites, organisations feminines et partenaires autour d'un meme objectif. Celui de faire de l'acces a l'eau un levier de developpement et d'emancipation pour les femmes. Au-dela de la commemoration, la rencontre a permis de dresser un etat des lieux des progres realises et des defis qui demeurent. Des progres enregistres Prenant la parole a l'ouverture de la ceremonie, la ministre de la promotion de la femme, de l'enfant et de la famille, Diarra Djeneba Sanogo, a reaffirme l'engagement du gouvernement a ameliorer l'acces des femmes a l'eau potable. Elle a presente les dernieres statistiques disponibles sur la couverture nationale. « En mars 2024, le taux d'acces au service de l'eau potable est de 83,2 % en milieu urbain et semi-urbain, contre 67,3 % en milieu rural, avec une moyenne nationale de 71,9 %. » Ces chiffres traduisent des avancees, mais mettent egalement en evidence l'ecart qui subsiste entre les villes et les campagnes. Dans les zones rurales, de nombreuses femmes continuent de consacrer une partie importante de leur temps a la recherche d'eau selon des organisations feminines. Les femmes demandent davantage d'infrastructures La presidente du Consortium des organisations feminines, Assitan Sidibe, a insiste sur la necessite de renforcer les infrastructures hydrauliques et les dispositifs d'assainissement dans la region de Koulikoro, voire partout dans le pays. « Malgre tout cela, nous avons besoin de forages pour que les femmes puissent s'approvisionner en eau. Nous avons aussi besoin de depots de transit ainsi que de depots finaux afin que tous les dechets soient transportes. » Selon elle, l'amelioration durable des conditions de vie des femmes passe egalement par un meilleur environnement sanitaire et une gestion plus efficace des dechets. L'autonomisation economique au cœur des revendications Au-dela de la question de l'eau, les participantes ont mis l'accent sur les conditions necessaires a une veritable autonomisation economique. Elles ont plaide pour un acces accru aux financements, aux formations professionnelles et aux activites generatrices de revenus. Ces appuis, estiment-elles, permettraient aux femmes de developper leurs activites, d'ameliorer leurs revenus et de renforcer leur contribution au developpement local. items.title: Court jails two Chinese nationals 25 years each for illegal mineral export
items.description: By Innocent Anaba Justice Akintayo Aluko of the Federal High Court in Lagos has convicted and sentenced two Chinese nationals, Zhang Hong Lin and Gao Pei Hai, to 25 years’ imprisonment each for offences related to the illegal export of Nigeria’s strategic mineral resources. The judge found the defendants guilty on all five counts filed against them by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), which included conspiracy, unlawful possession and attempted exportation of strategic minerals without lawful authority. Justice Aluko sentenced each defendant to 25 years’ imprisonment on each of the five counts, with an option of a ₦10 million fine on each count. He also ordered that the sentences take effect from the date of their arrest. In addition, the court ordered the forfeiture of all the mineral resources involved in the case to the Federal Government. The defendants were arraigned alongside a third suspect, Gao Pei Yu, who is currently at large. According to the charge filed before the court on May 28, 2025, the defendants allegedly conspired to defraud the Federal Government of revenue by attempting to export strategic mineral resources without the required authorisation. The prosecution alleged that the offences were committed in Lagos and contravened the provisions of the Miscellaneous Offences Act, 1983. The EFCC further accused the defendants of unlawfully possessing mineral resources intended for export without lawful authority. The minerals listed in the charge included mica minerals such as Muscovite and Lepidolite; lithium-bearing ores including Spodumene and Petalite; and other minerals associated with copper deposits, including Bornite and Cuprite, as well as Anhydrite, Quartz and Magnesite. After reviewing the evidence presented by the prosecution, Justice Aluko held that the EFCC had proved its case beyond reasonable doubt against the two convicted defendants and accordingly entered judgment against them.
